title.zh: 卷九十二 列傳第三十: 毛碩 李上達 曹望之 大懷貞 盧孝儉 盧庸 李偲 徒單克寧本名習顯
title.en: Volume 92 Biographies 30: Mao Shuo, Li Shangda, Cao Wangzhi, Da Huaizhen, Lu Xiaojian, Lu Yong, Li Cai, Tudan Kening Former Name Xixian
title.raw: 卷九十二 列傳第三十: 毛碩 李上達 曹望之 大懷貞 盧孝儉 盧庸 李偲 徒單克寧本名習顯 Volume 92 Biographies 30: Mao Shuo, Li Shangda, Cao Wangzhi, Da Huaizhen, Lu Xiaojian, Lu Yong, Li Cai, Tudan Kening Former Name Xixian

sentences.zh: 毛碩，字仲權，甘陵人。

translations.literal: Mao Shuo, courtesy name Zhongquan, was a native of Ganling.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Shuo, styled Zhongquan, came from Ganling.

sentences.zh: 宋末，試弓馬子弟，碩中選，調高陽關路安撫司準備差使。

translations.literal: At the end of the Song, when sons of officials were examined in archery and horsemanship, Shuo was selected and was assigned as a reserve appointee of the Gaoyang Pass Circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Song, Shuo passed the examination for sons of officials trained in archery and horsemanship and was posted as a standby assignee on the Gaoyang Pass Circuit Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 尋辟河間尉，再辟兵馬都監。

translations.literal: Soon he was recruited as magistrate of Hejian, and again as commander of military forces.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon commissioned as prefect of Hejian and then again as military commander.

sentences.zh: 宗望軍至，碩以本部迎降。

translations.literal: When Zongwang's army arrived, Shuo led his own command to welcome them and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zongwang's army arrived, Shuo brought his troops out to welcome them and submit.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，由淮東路第一副將擢知滑州。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was established, he was promoted from first deputy general of the Huaidong Circuit to magistrate of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was set up, he rose from first deputy general on the Huaidong Circuit to prefect of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 劉麟伐宋，充行營中軍統制軍馬。

translations.literal: When Liu Lin campaigned against the Song, he served as commander of cavalry and infantry in the central army of the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: During Liu Lin's campaign against the Song, he commanded the cavalry and infantry of the field headquarters' central army.

sentences.zh: 天眷間，曆汴京路、山東西路兵馬都監。

translations.literal: During the Tianjuan period he successively served as commander of military forces on the Bianjing Circuit and the Shandong West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianjuan era he served in turn as military commander on the Bianjing and Shandong West circuits.

sentences.zh: 皇統元年，權知拱州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangtong he served as acting magistrate of Gong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangtong (1141) he acted as prefect of Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋將張俊據亳州，而柘城酒監房人傑叛以應俊，碩發兵討之。

translations.literal: The Song general Zhang Jun held Bozhou, while Fang Renjie, supervisor of wine at Zhecheng, rebelled to support Jun; Shuo sent troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Zhang Jun held Bozhou, and Fang Renjie, the wine supervisor at Zhecheng, rebelled to join him; Shuo marched out to suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 至柘城，躬扣城門，呼耆老以諭意。

translations.literal: When he reached Zhecheng, he personally knocked on the city gate and summoned the elders to explain his intentions.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Zhecheng he went to the gate in person and called the elders to explain his purpose.

sentences.zh: 縣人縛人傑以降。

translations.literal: The people of the county bound Renjie and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The county people bound Renjie and submitted.

sentences.zh: 碩徑入縣署，召百姓慰安之，眾皆感悅，刻石紀其事。

translations.literal: Shuo went straight into the county office, summoned the people to comfort and reassure them, and all were moved and pleased; they carved a stone to record the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo entered the county seat at once, gathered the people to reassure them, and they were deeply grateful; a stone inscription was carved to commemorate the event.

sentences.zh: 四年，真授拱州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was formally appointed prefect of Gong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the reign he received formal appointment as prefect of Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 元帥梁王宗弼承制超武義將軍，改知曹州。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief, Prince of Liang Zongbi, by imperial order promoted him to Supervisory General of Wuyi and changed his post to magistrate of Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Prince of Liang Zongbi, acting on imperial authority, promoted him to Supervisory General of Wuyi and transferred him to prefect of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 有書生投書于碩，辭涉謗訕，僚屬皆不能堪。

translations.literal: A scholar submitted a letter to Shuo whose wording involved slander and ridicule; all his subordinates found it unbearable.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar sent Shuo a letter couched in insulting language; his staff could hardly bear it.

sentences.zh: 碩延之上座，謝曰：「使碩常聞斯言，庶乎寡過。」

translations.literal: Shuo invited him to the seat of honor and said in apology, "If Shuo could often hear such words, perhaps I might make fewer mistakes."
translations.idiomatic: Shuo seated him in the place of honor and said, "If I could hear such words regularly, I might commit fewer faults."

sentences.zh: 士論以故嘉之。

translations.literal: Men of letters for this reason praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 遷鄭州防禦使，尋改通州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture, and soon after was reassigned to Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to defense commissioner of Zhengzhou and soon transferred to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，充陝西路轉運使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande he served as transport commissioner of the Shaanxi West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tiande (1150) he became transport commissioner of the Shaanxi West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 碩以陝右邊荒，種藝不過麻、粟、蕎麥，賦入甚薄，市井交易惟川絹、幹薑，商賈不通，酒稅之入耗減，請視汴京、燕京例給交鈔通行。

translations.literal: Shuo observed that the Shaanxi right border region was desolate; crops were limited to hemp, millet, and buckwheat, tax revenue was very slight, market trade was only in Sichuan silk and dried ginger, merchants did not come and go, and wine-tax receipts dwindled; he requested that, following the precedents of Bianjing and Yanjing, paper notes be issued for circulation.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo noted that western Shaanxi was a frontier wasteland where farmers grew little beyond hemp, millet, and buckwheat, revenues were thin, markets traded mainly in Sichuan silk and dried ginger, merchants scarcely came, and wine taxes fell off; he asked that paper notes be issued for circulation there as at Bianjing and Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 而鞏、會、德順道路多險，鹽引斤數太重，請一引分作三四，以從輕便。

translations.literal: Moreover, the roads through Gong, Hui, and Deshun were mostly perilous, and the weight per salt certificate was too great; he requested that one certificate be divided into three or four to make transport easier.
translations.idiomatic: The routes through Gong, Hui, and Deshun were treacherous and salt certificates carried too much weight per unit; he proposed splitting each certificate into three or four parts to lighten the burden.

sentences.zh: 朝廷皆從之。

translations.literal: The court approved all of these proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved all his proposals.

sentences.zh: 秦州倉粟陳積，而百姓有支移者，止就本州折納其直，公私便之。

translations.literal: At Qin Prefecture grain in the granaries had aged, and for commoners who had transport obligations, payment was accepted only in cash at that prefecture at a converted rate, to the convenience of public and private interests alike.
translations.idiomatic: At Qinzhou the granaries held aged grain; for taxpayers liable for transport duties, he allowed cash payment at the local rate instead, which benefited both government and people.

sentences.zh: 改河東南路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to transport commissioner of the Hedong South Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as transport commissioner of the Hedong South Circuit.

sentences.zh: 上言：「頃者，定立商酒課，不量土產厚薄、戶口多寡及今昔物價之增耗，一概理責之，故監官被系，失身破家，折傭逃竄。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "Recently, when the commercial wine tax was fixed, no account was taken of whether local products were rich or poor, whether households were many or few, or whether prices had risen or fallen; a uniform levy was enforced. For this reason supervising officials were imprisoned, lost their persons and ruined their families, and hired laborers fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "When the commercial wine levy was recently fixed, no regard was paid to local productivity, population, or changes in prices; officials enforced a flat quota. Supervisors were arrested, families ruined, and hired workers fled.

sentences.zh: 或為奸吏盜有實錢，而以賒券輸官，故河東有積負至四百餘萬貫，公私苦之。

translations.literal: Sometimes corrupt clerks secretly kept the actual cash and paid the government with credit vouchers, so that in Hedong accumulated arrears reached more than four million strings, to the distress of public and private alike.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt clerks sometimes kept the cash and paid the government with credit notes, so that Hedong alone accumulated arrears of more than four million strings, to everyone's distress.

sentences.zh: 請自今禁約酒官，不得折准賒貸，惟許收用實錢，則官民俱便。」

translations.literal: He requested that from now on wine officials be forbidden to accept converted credit loans and be allowed to collect only real cash, so that government and people would both benefit."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that wine officials hereafter be barred from accepting credit conversions and required to take only cash, which would benefit both the state and the people."

sentences.zh: 至今行之。

translations.literal: This policy is still in force today.
translations.idiomatic: This policy remains in force to the present.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，除南京路都轉運使。

translations.literal: When his term expired he was appointed chief transport commissioner of the Nanjing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was appointed chief transport commissioner of the Nanjing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大定六年致仕，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dading he retired from office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dading (1166) he retired and died at home.

sentences.zh: 碩文雅好事，性謹飭，每見古人行事有益於時者，常書置座右，以為蒞官之戒雲。

translations.literal: Shuo was refined and fond of worthy pursuits, and by nature careful and disciplined; whenever he saw actions of the ancients beneficial to the age, he would often write them out and place them at his right hand as admonitions for holding office.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was cultivated and fond of good works, meticulous by nature; whenever he came upon ancient precedents useful for governance, he copied them and kept them at his desk as reminders for office.

sentences.zh: 李上達

translations.literal: Li Shangda
translations.idiomatic: Li Shangda

sentences.zh: 李上達，字達道，曹州濟陰人。

translations.literal: Li Shangda, courtesy name Dadao, was a native of Jiyin in Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shangda, styled Dadao, came from Jiyin in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 在宋時以廕補官，累東平府司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Under the Song he entered office by hereditary privilege and rose to registrar of the revenue section in Dongping Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song he entered service by yin privilege and eventually became revenue registrar in Dongping Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 撻懶取東平，上達給軍須，號辦治。

translations.literal: When Talan captured Dongping, Shangda supplied army provisions and was known for efficient administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Talan took Dongping, Shangda provisioned the army and was praised for his efficiency.

sentences.zh: 齊國建，為吏部員外郎，攝戶部事。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was established, he became vice director in the Ministry of Personnel and acted in charge of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was founded he became vice director in the Ministry of Personnel and handled Ministry of Revenue affairs.

sentences.zh: 劉豫行什一之法，樂歲輸多，歉歲寡取之，蓋古人助法也。

translations.literal: Liu Yu implemented the tithe method: in good years more was delivered, in lean years less was taken—this was essentially the ancient aid levy.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu applied the tithe system, taking more in good harvest years and less in bad—essentially the ancient mutual-aid levy.

sentences.zh: 收斂之時，蓄積蓋藏，民或不以實輸官，官亦不肯盡信，於是告訐起而獄訟繁，公私苦之。

translations.literal: At collection time people hoarded and concealed grain; commoners sometimes did not report the full amount to the government, and officials in turn were unwilling to trust them fully; informers arose, lawsuits multiplied, and public and private interests alike suffered.
translations.idiomatic: At harvest time people hoarded grain; peasants underreported and officials distrusted them; informers multiplied, lawsuits piled up, and everyone suffered.

sentences.zh: 上達論其弊，豫改定為五等之制。

translations.literal: Shangda discussed its abuses, and Yu revised it into a five-grade system.
translations.idiomatic: Shangda explained the abuses, and Yu replaced the system with five grades of assessment.

sentences.zh: 齊國廢，以河南與宋人，上達隨地入宋。

translations.literal: When the Qi state was abolished and Henan was given to the Song, Shangda followed the territory and entered Song service.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was abolished and Henan returned to the Song, Shangda went over with the territory.

sentences.zh: 宗弼複取河南，上達為同知大名尹，按察陝西、河南。

translations.literal: When Zongbi recovered Henan, Shangda became associate prefect of Daming and inspected Shaanxi and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongbi retook Henan, Shangda became associate prefect of Daming and conducted inspections in Shaanxi and Henan.

sentences.zh: 是時，關、陝、蒲、解、汝、蔡民饑，上達輒以便宜發倉粟賑百姓。

translations.literal: At that time the people of Guan, Shaan, Pu, Jie, Ru, and Cai were starving; Shangda repeatedly, as circumstances allowed, opened granaries to relieve the commoners.
translations.idiomatic: At that time famine struck Guanzhong, Shaanxi, Pu, Jie, Ru, and Cai; Shangda repeatedly opened granaries on his own authority to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 累遷知山東西路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to transport commissioner of the Shandong West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually appointed transport commissioner of the Shandong West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 上達到官再期，比舊增三十餘萬貫。

translations.literal: Within two terms after Shangda took office, receipts increased by more than three hundred thousand strings compared with before.
translations.idiomatic: Within two terms of his taking office, revenues rose by more than three hundred thousand strings over the previous level.

sentences.zh: 戶部以其法頒之鄰路。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue promulgated his methods to neighboring circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue extended his methods to neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 上達長於吏事，能治繁劇，猾吏不能欺，所至稱之。

translations.literal: Shangda excelled in administrative affairs, could handle heavy and complex duties, and crafty clerks could not deceive him; wherever he went he was praised.
translations.idiomatic: Shangda was skilled in administration, handled heavy workloads, and could not be fooled by corrupt clerks; he was praised wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 卒官，年六十一。

translations.literal: He died in office at the age of sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 曹望之

translations.literal: Cao Wangzhi
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wangzhi

sentences.zh: 曹望之，字景蕭，其先臨潢人，遼季移家宣德。

translations.literal: Cao Wangzhi, courtesy name Jingxiao, was originally from Linhuang; in the late Liao his family moved to Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wangzhi, styled Jingxiao, was descended from Linhuang; in the late Liao his family moved to Xuande.

sentences.zh: 天會間，以秀民子選充女直字學生。

translations.literal: During Tianhui he was selected as a Jurchen-script student from among sons of distinguished families.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianhui he was chosen from talented families to study the Jurchen script.

sentences.zh: 年十四，業成，除西京教授。

translations.literal: At fourteen he completed his studies and was appointed instructor at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he finished his course and was appointed instructor at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 為元帥府書令史，補正令史，轉行台省令史。

translations.literal: He served as a clerical secretary in the marshal's headquarters, was made a regular secretary, and was transferred to secretary of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a clerical secretary in the marshal's headquarters, was promoted to regular secretary, and then transferred to the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 錄教授資，補修武校尉，除右司都事。

translations.literal: His instructor's qualifications were recorded, he was appointed Repair-the-Army Commandant, and was made chief clerk of the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: His teaching service was credited, he was appointed Repair-the-Army Commandant, and made chief clerk of the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎田玨素薄望之，望之願交不肯納，遂與蔡松年、許霖構致黨獄。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Tian Jue had long slighted Wangzhi; Wangzhi wished to associate with him but Jue would not accept him, whereupon together with Cai Songnian and Xu Lin they engineered a faction case against him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Tian Jue had long looked down on Wangzhi, who sought his friendship in vain; Tian then joined Cai Songnian and Xu Lin in framing him in a faction case.

sentences.zh: 改行台吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as vice director in the Branch Secretariat's Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as vice director of personnel in the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大定初，討窩斡，望之主軍食，給與有節，凡省糧三十萬石，省剉草五十萬石。

translations.literal: In the early Dading period, when Wohela was being suppressed, Wangzhi was in charge of army provisions; his distribution was measured, and in all he saved three hundred thousand piculs of grain and five hundred thousand piculs of chopped fodder.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading, during the campaign against Wohela, Wangzhi managed army rations with restraint, saving three hundred thousand piculs of grain and five hundred thousand piculs of fodder in all.

sentences.zh: 帥府以捷入告，議者欲遂罷轉輸，望之以為元惡未誅，不可弛備。

translations.literal: The command reported victory to the court; some at court wished to halt transport at once, but Wangzhi held that the chief villain had not yet been executed and preparations must not be relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: When headquarters reported victory, some urged stopping supply convoys, but Wangzhi argued that the chief rebel was not yet dead and vigilance must not slacken.

sentences.zh: 既而大軍追討，果賴以濟。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the main army pursued and attacked, and indeed relied on this to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army pursued the rebels, it indeed depended on those supplies to prevail.

sentences.zh: 以勞進一階，兼同修國史。

translations.literal: For his merit he was advanced one rank and concurrently made co-compiler of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted one rank and appointed co-compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 請於大鹽濼設官榷鹽，聽民以米貿易，民成聚落，可以固邊圉，其利無窮。

translations.literal: He requested that at the Great Salt Marsh an office be set up to monopolize salt and allow the people to trade in grain; the people would form settlements, the border could be secured, and the benefit would be boundless.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed establishing a government salt monopoly at the Great Salt Marsh and letting people trade grain for salt, so that settlements would grow and secure the frontier—a measure of boundless benefit.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 其後凡貯米二十余萬石。

translations.literal: Afterward grain stored there totaled more than two hundred thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually more than two hundred thousand piculs of grain were stored there.

sentences.zh: 及東北路歲饑，賴以濟者不可勝數。

translations.literal: When the Northeast Circuit suffered famine in successive years, those who were saved by it were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In later years of famine on the Northeast Circuit, countless people were saved by those stores.

sentences.zh: 三年，上曰：「自正隆兵興，農桑失業，猛安謀克屯田多不如法。」

translations.literal: In the third year the emperor said, "Since military campaigns began in Zhenglong, agriculture and sericulture have been disrupted, and military colony farming by military colonies is often not conducted according to regulations."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the emperor said, "Since the wars of Zhenglong, farming has been disrupted, and military colony settlements are often mismanaged."

sentences.zh: 詔遣戶部侍郎魏子平、大興少尹同知中都轉運事李滌、禮部侍郎李願、禮部郎中移剌道、戶部員外郎完顏兀古出、監察禦史夾谷阿裏補及望之分道勸農，廉問職官臧否。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Vice Minister of Revenue Wei Ziping, Vice Prefect of Daxing and associate transport commissioner of the Central Capital Li Di, Vice Minister of Rites Li Yuan, Director in the Ministry of Rites Yelü Dao, Vice Director of Revenue Wanyan Wugu, Supervising Censor Jiagu Alibu, and Wangzhi by separate routes to encourage agriculture and to investigate the merit and faults of officials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Vice Minister Wei Ziping, Vice Prefect Li Di, Vice Minister Li Yuan, Director Yelü Dao, Vice Director Wanyan Wugu, Censor Jiagu Alibu, and Wangzhi on separate routes to promote farming and investigate officials' conduct.

sentences.zh: 望之還言，乞汰諸路胥吏，可減其半。

translations.literal: On his return Wangzhi reported, requesting that clerks on all circuits be culled, by as much as half.
translations.idiomatic: On returning, Wangzhi proposed cutting circuit clerks by half.

sentences.zh: 詔胥吏如故。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that clerks remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: An edict left the clerical staff unchanged.

sentences.zh: 於是始禁用貼書雲。

translations.literal: At this time the use of attached clerks was first forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the use of attached clerks was first banned.

sentences.zh: 遷本部侍郎，領複實繕修大內財用，費用大省。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of his department and took charge of verifying and repairing the inner palace's finances; expenditures were greatly reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of his department and oversaw verification and repairs in the inner palace, greatly reducing costs.

sentences.zh: 複以勞進階，上召見諭勉之。

translations.literal: Again for his merit he was advanced in rank; the emperor summoned him and exhorted him with encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Again rewarded for his service with a promotion, he was summoned and encouraged by the emperor.

sentences.zh: 望之家奴袁一言涉妖妄，大興府鞫治。

translations.literal: Wangzhi's household slave Yuan spoke words involving sorcery and delusion; the Daxing prefecture investigated and tried the case.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi's household slave Yuan made statements involving sorcery; the Daxing prefecture tried the case.

sentences.zh: 望之恐，使戶部令史劉公輔問其事于大興少尹王全，全具其事語公輔，公輔以語望之。

translations.literal: Wangzhi was afraid and sent Ministry of Revenue secretary Liu Gongfu to inquire about the matter from Vice Prefect of Daxing Wang Quan; Quan told Gongfu the full affair, and Gongfu told Wangzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing exposure, Wangzhi sent revenue secretary Liu Gongfu to ask Vice Prefect Wang Quan about the case; Quan told him everything, and Gongfu relayed it to Wangzhi.

sentences.zh: 禦史台劾奏劉公輔言泄獄情。

translations.literal: The Censorate impeached Liu Gongfu for leaking details of the prison case.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate impeached Liu Gongfu for leaking details of the investigation.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「妖妄之言，交相傳說何也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Why are deluded words being passed back and forth?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Why are such deluded rumors being passed around?"

sentences.zh: 於是，望之決杖一百，王全杖八十，劉公輔杖一百五十，除名。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wangzhi was sentenced to one hundred strokes with the rod, Wang Quan to eighty strokes, and Liu Gongfu to one hundred fifty strokes and dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi was sentenced to one hundred strokes, Wang Quan to eighty, and Liu Gongfu to one hundred fifty strokes and dismissal from office.

sentences.zh: 頃之，運河堙塞，世宗出郊見之，問其故。

translations.literal: Before long the Grand Canal was silted and blocked; Emperor Shizong went out to the suburbs, saw it, and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Grand Canal silted up; Emperor Shizong saw it on an outing and asked why.

sentences.zh: 主者奏曰：「戶部不肯經畫，歲久以致如此。」

translations.literal: Those in charge reported, "The Ministry of Revenue would not undertake planning; over the years it has come to this."
translations.idiomatic: Those responsible reported, "The Ministry of Revenue would not plan maintenance, and over the years it came to this."

sentences.zh: 上責望之曰：「有水運不浚治，乃用陸運，煩費民力，罪在汝等，其往治之。」

translations.literal: The emperor reproached Wangzhi: "When water transport is available you do not dredge and maintain it, yet use land transport instead, wasting the people's strength—the fault lies with you and your kind; go and repair it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Wangzhi: "With water transport available you failed to dredge the canal and forced costly land transport on the people—the fault is yours; go and fix it."

sentences.zh: 尚書省奏當用夫役數萬人。

translations.literal: The Imperial Secretariat memorialized that several tens of thousands of laborers would be needed.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Secretariat reported that tens of thousands of laborers would be needed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「方春耕作，不可勞民。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "It is now the season of spring plowing; the people must not be overburdened.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Spring planting is underway; the people must not be overburdened.

sentences.zh: 以宮籍監戶及摘東宮、諸王人從充役，若不足即以五百里內軍夫補之。」

translations.literal: Use palace-register supervised households and detach attendants from the Eastern Palace and the princes for labor; if that is insufficient, supplement with military laborers from within five hundred li."
translations.idiomatic: Use palace-register households and detach attendants from the crown prince and princes for labor; if that is not enough, supplement with military corvée within five hundred li."

sentences.zh: 《太宗實錄》成，監修國史紇石烈良弼賜金帶一、重彩二十端。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizong were completed, supervising compiler of the national history Hešilie Liangbi was granted one gold belt and twenty bolts of heavy silk.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizong were completed, supervising compiler Hešilie Liangbi received a gold belt and twenty bolts of heavy silk.

sentences.zh: 同修國史張景仁、劉仲淵、望之皆賜銀幣有差。

translations.literal: Co-compilers Zhang Jingren, Liu Zhongyuan, and Wangzhi were all granted silver and coins in varying amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Co-compilers Zhang Jingren, Liu Zhongyuan, and Wangzhi received silver and coins in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 望之歎賞薄，謂人曰：「栽花接本乃加爵命，勤勞者不遷官。」

translations.literal: Wangzhi sighed that the reward was meager and said to others, "Those who plant flowers and graft trees receive ennoblement, while those who labor diligently receive no promotion in office."
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi complained that the reward was stingy and said, "Gardeners who graft flowers get titles, while those who work hard get no promotion."

sentences.zh: 無何，張景仁遷翰林學士，望之又曰：「止與他人便遣，獨不及我哉。」

translations.literal: Before long Zhang Jingren was transferred to Hanlin academician, and Wangzhi again said, "They give convenient appointments only to others—why not to me?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhang Jingren was made Hanlin academician, and Wangzhi grumbled again, "They hand out easy posts to everyone but me."

sentences.zh: 世宗聞之，出望之德州防禦使，謂之曰：「汝為人能幹而心不忠實。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong heard of this, he sent Wangzhi out as defense commissioner of De Prefecture and said to him, "You are capable in your work but your heart is not loyal and sincere.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong heard this, he sent Wangzhi out as defense commissioner of Dezhou and told him, "You are capable but not loyal at heart.

sentences.zh: 朕前往安州春水，人言汝無事君之義。

translations.literal: When I went before to An Prefecture for the spring hunt, people said you lacked the duty owed a ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When I went to Anzhou for the spring hunt, people said you showed no loyalty to your ruler.

sentences.zh: 朕敕臣下，有過即當諫爭。

translations.literal: I have instructed my ministers that when there are faults they should remonstrate at once.
translations.idiomatic: I have told my ministers to remonstrate when they see fault.

sentences.zh: 汝但面從，退則謗議，此不忠不孝也。

translations.literal: You only agree to my face and slander behind my back—this is disloyalty and unfilial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: You agree to my face and slander me behind my back—that is disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 汝自五品起遷四品，《太宗皇帝實錄》成，優賜銀幣，不思盡心竭力，惟官賞是覬。

translations.literal: You rose from the fifth rank to the fourth; when the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizong were completed you were generously given silver and coins, yet you do not think to exhaust your heart and strength—you only covet office and reward.
translations.idiomatic: You rose from fifth to fourth rank; when the Taizong Veritable Records were finished you were generously rewarded, yet you give no full loyalty—you only crave office and gifts.

sentences.zh: 今出汝於外，宜改心滌慮。

translations.literal: Now that I am sending you outside the capital, you should reform your heart and cleanse your thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I am sending you away, reform your heart and mind.

sentences.zh: 不然，則身亦莫保。」

translations.literal: Otherwise you will not even preserve your person."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise you may not even keep your life."

sentences.zh: 望之到德州，有惠政，百姓為立生祠。

translations.literal: When Wangzhi reached De Prefecture he enacted benevolent policies, and the common people erected a living shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: At Dezhou Wangzhi governed well, and the people erected a living shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 改同知西京留守事。

translations.literal: He was changed to associate military commissioner of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed associate military commissioner of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 上書論便宜事：其一，論山東、河北猛安謀克與百姓雜處，民多失業。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial discussing expedient measures: first, on the ming'an and mouk'o military colonies of Shandong and Hebei living intermingled with commoners, so that many people lost their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on practical reforms: first, that in Shandong and Hebei military colonists lived among commoners, leaving many peasants without livelihood.

sentences.zh: 陳、蔡、汝、潁之間土廣人稀，宜徙百姓以實其處，複數年之賦以安輯之。

translations.literal: Between Chen, Cai, Ru, and Ying the land was broad and the people sparse; commoners should be relocated to fill those places, and several years' taxes remitted to settle and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Between Chen, Cai, Ru, and Ying the land was broad and sparsely settled; he proposed resettling peasants there and remitting several years' taxes to settle them.

sentences.zh: 百姓亡命及避役軍中者，閱實其人，使還本貫。

translations.literal: For commoners who had fled as outlaws or evaded corvée by joining the army, their persons should be verified and they should be made to return to their original domiciles.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives and those hiding in the army to evade corvée should be identified and sent back to their home registers.

sentences.zh: 或編近縣以為客戶，或留為佃戶者，亦籍其姓名。

translations.literal: Those enrolled in nearby counties as client households, or kept on as tenant farmers, should also have their names registered.
translations.idiomatic: Those enrolled as clients in nearby counties or kept on as tenant farmers should also be registered by name.

sentences.zh: 州縣與猛安事干涉者無相黨匿，庶幾軍民協和，盜賊弭息。

translations.literal: When prefectures and counties and military colonies interfered in one another's affairs they should not shield one another; then perhaps military and civilians would be harmonious and banditry would cease.
translations.idiomatic: When prefectures and military colonies interfered in each other's affairs they should not cover for one another, so that soldiers and civilians might live in harmony and banditry subside.

sentences.zh: 其二，論薦舉之法虛文無實。

translations.literal: Second, on the recommendation system being empty form without substance.
translations.idiomatic: Second, he argued that the recommendation system was empty form without substance.

sentences.zh: 宰相拔擢及其所識，不及其所不識。

translations.literal: Chancellors promoted those they knew and did not reach those they did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors promoted only those they knew and overlooked those they did not.

sentences.zh: 內外官所舉亦輒不用，或指以為朋黨，遂不敢複舉。

translations.literal: Recommendations from inner and outer officials were also often not used, or were denounced as factional ties, so people no longer dared to recommend.
translations.idiomatic: Recommendations from court and local officials were often ignored or branded as factionalism, so officials ceased recommending anyone.

sentences.zh: 宜令宰執歲舉三品二人，御史大夫以下內外官終秩舉二人，自此以下以品殺為差等。

translations.literal: It should be ordered that the chief ministers each year recommend two persons of the third rank, and that inner and outer officials from the censor-in-chief down, at the end of their terms, each recommend two persons, with graded quotas below that according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that chief ministers recommend two third-rank officials annually, and that officials from the censor-in-chief down each recommend two at term's end, with lower ranks assigned proportionally reduced quotas.

sentences.zh: 終秩不舉者遇轉官勒不遷，三品者削後任俸三月。

translations.literal: Those who at term's end did not recommend anyone, when their turn for transfer came, would be compelled not to advance; third-rank officials would have three months' salary of their next post cut.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who failed to recommend at term's end would be blocked from promotion; third-rank officials would forfeit three months' salary from their next appointment.

sentences.zh: 其舉者已改除，吏部以類品第，季而上之。

translations.literal: When those recommended had already received new appointments, the Ministry of Personnel would rank them by category and report upward each season.
translations.idiomatic: Once nominees were appointed elsewhere, the Ministry of Personnel would rank them by category and report quarterly.

sentences.zh: 三品闕則於類第四品中補授，四品五品以下視此為差。

translations.literal: When third-rank posts were vacant, appointment would be made from fourth-rank candidates in the same category; fourth and fifth ranks and below would follow this pattern with appropriate differences.
translations.idiomatic: Vacant third-rank posts would be filled from fourth-rank candidates in the same category, with similar rules for lower ranks.

sentences.zh: 其待以不次者，宰執具才行功實以聞。

translations.literal: For those to be treated with extraordinary promotion, the chief ministers should set forth talent, conduct, and achievements in fact and report them.
translations.idiomatic: For exceptional promotion, chief ministers should report the candidate's talent, conduct, and achievements in detail.

sentences.zh: 舉當否罪當如律。

translations.literal: Whether recommendations were appropriate and guilt should follow the law.
translations.idiomatic: Appropriate and inappropriate recommendations, and corresponding penalties, should follow the law.

sentences.zh: 廉介之士老於令幕無舉主者、七考無贓私罪者，准朝官三考勞敘。

translations.literal: Upright men who had grown old in magistrates' staffs without a patron, and those with seven evaluations and no corruption offenses, should be granted merit promotion as court officials receive after three evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: Honest officials long serving in magistrates' staffs without patrons, and those with seven evaluations and no corruption convictions, should receive merit promotion like court officials after three evaluations.

sentences.zh: 吏部每季圖上外路職官姓名，路為一圖，大書贓汙者於其名下，使知畏慎。

translations.literal: Each season the Ministry of Personnel should chart the names of outer-circuit officials, one chart per circuit, and write large beneath the names of those guilty of corruption, so that they would know fear and caution.
translations.idiomatic: Each quarter the Ministry of Personnel should publish charts of outer-circuit officials by circuit, prominently marking corrupt officials beneath their names to inspire caution.

sentences.zh: 外任五品以上官改除，令代之者具功過以聞。

translations.literal: When outer officials of the fifth rank and above were reassigned, their successors should report their merits and faults.
translations.idiomatic: When fifth-rank and higher outer officials were reassigned, their successors should report their merits and faults to the court.

sentences.zh: 年六十以上者，終更赴調，有司察其視聽精力，老疾不堪厘務，給以半祿罷遣。

translations.literal: For those sixty years and above, at the end of their term they would report for reassignment; the relevant offices would examine their sight, hearing, and energy; if old age and illness made them unfit for duties, they would be given half salary and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Officials over sixty, at term's end, would report for reassignment; if examination showed age or illness unfit for duty, they would receive half salary and be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 其三，論守邊將帥及沿邊州縣官漁剝軍民，擅興力役，宜歲遣監察禦史周行察之。

translations.literal: Third, on frontier generals and border prefecture and county officials who preyed on soldiers and civilians and arbitrarily imposed corvée: each year supervising censors should be dispatched to tour and investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Third, frontier generals and border officials who exploited soldiers and civilians and imposed unauthorized corvée should be inspected annually by touring supervising censors.

sentences.zh: 邊部有訟，招討司無得輒遣白身人征斷，宜於省部有出身女直、契丹人及縣令丞簿中擇廉能者，因其風俗，略定科條，務為簡易。

translations.literal: When there were lawsuits in the border regions, the pacification commission must not casually send unranked persons to judge and decide; from the central ministries one should select capable Jurchen and Khitan officials with formal rank, and from magistrates, assistants, and registrars, choose the honest and able; according to local custom, statutes should be broadly set, kept simple.
translations.idiomatic: Border lawsuits should not be judged by unranked agents of the pacification commission; honest, capable ranked Jurchen, Khitan, and county officials should be chosen to set simple statutes suited to local custom.

sentences.zh: 征斷羊馬入官籍數，如邊部遇饑饉，即以此賑給之。

translations.literal: Sheep and horses adjudicated in lawsuits should be entered in government registers; if the border regions encountered famine, they should be used for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Sheep and horses from adjudicated cases should be registered; in border famine they should be used for relief.

sentences.zh: 招討及都監視事，宜限邊部饋送駝馬。

translations.literal: For pacification commissioners and commanders overseeing affairs, border gifts of camels and horses should be limited.
translations.idiomatic: Gifts of camels and horses to pacification commissioners and military overseers from the border should be limited.

sentences.zh: 招討司女直人戶，或擷野菜以濟艱食，而軍中舊籍馬死，則一村均錢補買，往往鬻妻子、賣耕牛以備之。

translations.literal: Among Jurchen households under the pacification commission, some gathered wild vegetables to survive hardship; when registered army horses died, the whole village shared the cost to replace them, and often sold wives and children or plow oxen to meet it.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchen households under the pacification commission sometimes gathered wild plants to survive; when registered army horses died, the whole village shared replacement costs, often selling wives, children, or oxen to pay.

sentences.zh: 臣恐數年之後，邊防困弊，臨時賑濟，費財十倍而無益，早為之所，則財用省而邊備實矣。

translations.literal: Your subject fears that after several years the frontier defenses will be exhausted; emergency relief would cost ten times the expense without benefit; if action is taken early, expenditures will be saved and frontier defenses made solid.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that in a few years the frontier will be exhausted; emergency relief would cost ten times as much to little purpose—early action would save funds and strengthen defenses.

sentences.zh: 官給軍箭用盡，則市以補之，皆朽鈍不堪用，可每歲給官箭一分，以補其闕。

translations.literal: When government-issue military arrows were used up, they were bought on the market to replenish them, but all were rotten and blunt and unusable; each year one-tenth of official arrows could be issued to make up the shortage.
translations.idiomatic: When government arrows were exhausted, market replacements were rotten and useless; he proposed issuing one-tenth of the official quota annually to fill the gap.

sentences.zh: 邊民闕食給米，地遠負重，往往就倉賤賣而去，可計口支錢，則公私兩便。

translations.literal: When border people lacked food they were given grain; the distance made transport burdensome, and they often sold it cheaply at the granary and left; payment by head count in cash would benefit both public and private interests.
translations.idiomatic: Border people given famine grain often sold it cheaply at the granary because transport was costly; cash payment by head count would benefit both state and people.

sentences.zh: 陝西正副，宜如猛安謀克用土人一員，隊將亦宜參用土人，久居其任。

translations.literal: For chief and deputy commanders in Shaanxi, as with military colonies one local man should be used; squad leaders should also include local men and hold office for long terms.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi commanders, like military colony officers, should include one local man; squad leaders should also include locals serving long terms.

sentences.zh: 增弓箭田，複其賦役。

translations.literal: Increase bow-and-arrow fields and restore their tax and corvée exemptions.
translations.idiomatic: Increase archery fields and restore their tax and corvée exemptions.

sentences.zh: 以廉吏為提舉，舉察總管府以下官。

translations.literal: Appoint honest officials as inspectors to investigate officials from the general command down.
translations.idiomatic: Honest officials should be appointed inspectors to investigate officials from the general command down.

sentences.zh: 農隙校閱，以嚴武備。

translations.literal: In agricultural slack seasons conduct reviews to tighten military preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: In slack farming seasons conduct drills to tighten military readiness.

sentences.zh: 則太平之時有經略之制矣。

translations.literal: Then in times of peace there would be a system of frontier strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Then even in peace there would be a system of frontier strategy.

sentences.zh: 又論六鹽場用人，宜令戶部公議辟舉。

translations.literal: He also discussed staffing the six salt fields: the Ministry of Revenue should openly deliberate and commission appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed that the Ministry of Revenue openly deliberate and commission staff for the six salt fields.

sentences.zh: 論漕運，先計河倉見在幾何，通州容受幾何，京師歲費幾何。

translations.literal: On grain transport, one should first calculate how much was presently in river granaries, how much Tong Prefecture could hold, and how much the capital consumed yearly.
translations.idiomatic: On grain transport, he proposed first calculating stocks in river granaries, Tongzhou's capacity, and the capital's annual consumption.

sentences.zh: 今近河州縣歲稅或六七萬石，小民有入資之費，富室收轉輸之利，宜計實數以科稅入。

translations.literal: Now the yearly tax of nearby river prefectures and counties might be sixty or seventy thousand piculs; commoners had costs of contributing capital, and wealthy households reaped profits from transport; the actual amount should be calculated for tax delivery.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby river districts paid sixty or seventy thousand piculs yearly in tax; commoners bore capital costs while the wealthy profited from transport—taxes should be assessed on actual amounts.

sentences.zh: 論民間私錢苦惡，宜以官錢五百易私錢千，期以一月易之，過期以銷錢法坐之。

translations.literal: On the people's private coin being bitterly debased: official coin at five hundred should be exchanged for one thousand private coins, with a one-month deadline; after the deadline the law on destroying coin should apply.
translations.idiomatic: On debased private coin, he proposed exchanging five hundred official coins for one thousand private coins within one month, with penalties for delay under the coin-destruction law.

sentences.zh: 論州府力役錢物，戶部頒印署白簿，使盡書之，以俟審閱，有畏避不書者坐之。

translations.literal: On corvée money and goods of prefectures and circuits: the Ministry of Revenue should issue sealed white registers for full recording, pending audit; those who feared and avoided recording should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: On prefectural corvée funds, the Ministry of Revenue should issue sealed registers for full recording; those who refused to record should be punished.

sentences.zh: 論工部營造調發，妨民生業。

translations.literal: On the Ministry of Works' construction levies harming the people's livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: On Ministry of Works construction levies harming people's livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 諸路射糧軍約量人數，習武藝，期以三年成，以息調民。

translations.literal: On all circuits' grain-shooting soldiers, estimate the numbers, train in martial arts, expect completion in three years, and thereby ease levies on the people.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed estimating grain-shooting soldiers on all circuits, training them in three years, and thereby easing levies on the people.

sentences.zh: 書奏，多見採納。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, much of it was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his memorial was adopted.

sentences.zh: 以本官行六部事於北邊，召拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: With his original rank he handled the affairs of the Six Ministries on the northern frontier and was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: While retaining his rank he managed Six Ministry affairs on the northern frontier, then was summoned as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 上數之曰：「汝前為侍郎，以不忠外補，頗能練習錢谷，故任以尚書之重，宜改前非，以圖新效也。」

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly told him: "You were previously a vice minister and were sent outside for disloyalty; you are quite practiced in revenue and grain, so I entrust you with the weight of minister; you should reform your former faults and strive for new achievement."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him: "As vice minister you were sent out for disloyalty; you know revenue well, so I give you the ministry—reform your faults and prove yourself anew."

sentences.zh: 是時，戶部尚書高德基坐高估俸粟責降，世宗念望之吝出納或懲德基也，既出，使人諭之曰：「勿以高德基下粟直，要在平估而已。」

translations.literal: At that time Minister of Revenue Gao Deji was demoted for overvaluing salary grain; Emperor Shizong thought Wangzhi's stinginess in disbursement might have been meant to punish Deji; after he left, he sent someone to instruct him: "Do not follow Gao Deji in lowering grain prices; what matters is fair valuation."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Gao Deji had been demoted for overvaluing salary grain; the emperor, thinking Wangzhi's stinginess might have targeted Deji, sent word: "Do not lower grain prices as Deji did—keep valuations fair."

sentences.zh: 十五年新宮成，世宗幸新宮，敕望之曰：「新宮中所須，毋取於民間也。」

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the new palace was completed; Emperor Shizong visited the new palace and ordered Wangzhi: "What the new palace needs must not be taken from the people."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, when the new palace was completed, the emperor ordered Wangzhi: "Take nothing from the people for the new palace."

sentences.zh: 有良民夫婦質身于東京留守完顏彀英家，期終而不遣，尚書省下東京鞫治。

translations.literal: A worthy commoner couple pledged themselves to the household of Eastern Capital military commissioner Wanyan Guying; when the term ended they were not released; the Imperial Secretariat ordered Eastern Capital to investigate and try the case.
translations.idiomatic: A worthy couple pledged to Eastern Capital commissioner Wanyan Guying's household; when the term ended he would not release them; the Imperial Secretariat ordered an investigation in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 望之言彀英為留守，其同官必且阿徇，不肯窮竟，當移他州。

translations.literal: Wangzhi said that since Guying was military commissioner, his colleagues would certainly curry favor and would not pursue the matter to the end; the case should be moved to another prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi said Guying's colleagues would cover for him and the case should be transferred to another prefecture.

sentences.zh: 望之久習事，有治錢谷名，性剛愎，頗沾沾自露，希覬執政。

translations.literal: Wangzhi had long been practiced in affairs and had a reputation for managing revenue and grain; by nature he was stubborn and willful, rather self-displaying, and hoped for a place in government.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi was experienced in administration and renowned for revenue management, but was stubborn, self-promoting, and coveted high office.

sentences.zh: 而刑部尚書梁肅自詳問宋國使還，世宗嘗欲以為執政，久而未用，亦頗炫耀求進。

translations.literal: Minister of Punishments Liang Su, returning from detailed inquiry of the Song envoy, had once been considered by Emperor Shizong for government, but after long delay was not used and also rather showed off seeking advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Liang Su, returning from interrogating the Song envoy, had long been considered for high office but was passed over and also sought advancement conspicuously.

sentences.zh: 世宗謂左丞相紇石烈良弼日：「曹望之、梁肅急於見知，涉於躁進。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong said to Left Chancellor Hešilie Liangbi one day: "Cao Wangzhi and Liang Su are eager to be known and verge on rash advancement."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Left Chancellor Hešilie Liangbi: "Cao Wangzhi and Liang Su are too eager for recognition and verge on rash advancement."

sentences.zh: 遂出梁肅為濟南尹。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liang Su was sent out as prefect of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Su was sent out as prefect of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 數年，乃召拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Several years later he was summoned and appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Liang Su was summoned as Vice Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 而望之終於戶部尚書，年五十六。

translations.literal: But Wangzhi ended his career as Minister of Revenue at the age of fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi ended his career as Minister of Revenue at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 世宗惜其未及用，賜錢三千貫，敕使致祭，賻銀五百兩、重彩二十端、絹二百匹，以其子淵為奉禦，澤為筆硯承奉。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong regretted that he had not been fully used, granted three thousand strings of cash, ordered an envoy to perform sacrifices, gave five hundred taels of silver for funeral expenses, twenty bolts of heavy silk, and two hundred bolts of silk; his son Yuan was made palace attendant and Ze made brush-and-ink attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regretted not using him fully, granted three thousand strings of cash, ordered sacrifices, gave five hundred taels of silver, twenty bolts of heavy silk, and two hundred bolts of silk; his sons Yuan and Ze received palace appointments.

sentences.zh: 其後，尚輦局舉出身人年六十餘可以臨事，世宗曰：「豈為此輩惜官邪，但此輩專以盜取官錢為謀生計，不可用也。」

translations.literal: Afterward the Palace Transport Bureau recommended a man over sixty with formal rank who could handle affairs; the emperor said, "Would I spare office for such people? But these people specialize in stealing official funds as their livelihood and cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: Later the Palace Transport Bureau recommended a man over sixty fit for office; the emperor said, "I would not spare office for them—but they live by stealing official funds and are unusable."

sentences.zh: 由是欲更改監臨格式，以問戶部尚書劉瑋。

translations.literal: For this reason he wished to revise the format for supervising offices and asked Minister of Revenue Liu Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore wished to revise supervisory regulations and consulted Minister Liu Wei.

sentences.zh: 瑋恐監官謗己，不肯實對。

translations.literal: Wei feared that supervising officials would slander him and would not answer truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wei, fearing slander from supervisors, would not answer honestly.

sentences.zh: 世宗因思望之，歎曰：「不如望之之敢行也。」

translations.literal: The emperor then thought of Wangzhi and sighed, "He was not as bold in action as Wangzhi."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sighed, "He was not as bold as Wangzhi."

sentences.zh: 望之初不學，及貴，稍知讀書，遂刻苦自致，有詩集三十卷。

translations.literal: At first Wangzhi did not study; after he became eminent he gradually learned to read and then applied himself strenuously, and had a poetry collection in thirty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi had not studied early in life; after rising high he taught himself to read, applied himself diligently, and left a poetry collection in thirty juan.

sentences.zh: 大懷貞

translations.literal: Da Huaizhen
translations.idiomatic: Da Huaizhen

sentences.zh: 大懷貞，字子正，遼陽人。

translations.literal: Da Huaizhen, courtesy name Zizheng, was a native of Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Da Huaizhen, styled Zizheng, came from Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 皇統五年，除閤門祗候，三遷東上閣門使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huangtong he was appointed gate usher; after three promotions he became eastern upper gate commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Huangtong he became a gate usher and after three promotions was eastern upper gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起複符寶郎，累官右宣徽使。

translations.literal: When his mother's mourning ended he returned to service as talisman attendant and rose to Right Palace Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he returned as talisman attendant and rose to Right Palace Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 正隆伐宋，為武勝軍都總管。

translations.literal: During the Zhenglong campaign against the Song he was overall commander of the Wusheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenglong campaign against the Song he commanded the Wusheng Army.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，除洺州防禦使兼押軍萬戶，改沂州，再遷彰國、安武軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he was appointed defense commissioner of Luozhou and concurrently commander of the ten-thousand households; he was transferred to Yizhou, then promoted to military commissioners of Zhangguo and Anwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading he became defense commissioner of Luozhou and commander of ten thousand households, then transferred to Yizhou and promoted to military commissioner of Zhangguo and Anwu.

sentences.zh: 縣尉獲盜，得一旗，上圖亢宿。

translations.literal: The county constable caught a bandit and obtained a banner on which the constellation Kang was depicted.
translations.idiomatic: A county constable caught bandits and found a banner depicting the Kang constellation.

sentences.zh: 詰之，有謀叛狀，株連幾萬人。

translations.literal: On interrogation there was evidence of plotting rebellion; tens of thousands were implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation revealed a rebellion plot; tens of thousands were implicated.

sentences.zh: 懷貞當以亂民之刑，請誅其首亂者十八人，餘皆釋之。

translations.literal: Huaizhen should have applied the penalty for disturbing the people; he requested execution of the eighteen chief instigators and released the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen should have punished the disturbance wholesale; he executed eighteen ringleaders and released the rest.

sentences.zh: 嘗以私忌飯僧數人，就中一僧異常，懷貞問曰：「汝何許人也？」

translations.literal: Once on a private taboo day he fed several monks, and among them one monk was unusual; Huaizhen asked, "Where are you from?"
translations.idiomatic: Once on a private memorial day he fed several monks; one seemed unusual, and Huaizhen asked, "Where are you from?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「山西人。」

translations.literal: He answered, "From Shanxi."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "From Shanxi."

sentences.zh: 複問：「曾為盜殺人否？」

translations.literal: He asked again, "Have you ever robbed and killed?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "Have you ever robbed and killed?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「無之。」

translations.literal: He answered, "No."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "No."

sentences.zh: 後三日詰盜，果引此僧，皆服其明察。

translations.literal: Three days later when bandits were interrogated, they indeed implicated this monk; all admired his keen perception.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later, interrogating bandits, they implicated this monk; all admired his perceptiveness.

sentences.zh: 改興中尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Xingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Xingzhong.

sentences.zh: 錦州富民蕭鶴壽途中殺人，匿府少尹家，有司捕不得，懷貞以計取之，置於法。

translations.literal: The wealthy man of Jin Prefecture Xiao Heshou killed someone on the road and hid in the home of the associate prefect; officials could not arrest him; Huaizhen took him by stratagem and punished him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy Jinzhou man Xiao Heshou killed someone on the road and hid with the associate prefect; officials could not catch him; Huaizhen seized him by stratagem and punished him.

sentences.zh: 改彰德軍節度使，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of Zhangde Army and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner of Zhangde Army and died.

sentences.zh: 盧孝儉

translations.literal: Lu Xiaojian
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiaojian

sentences.zh: 盧孝儉，宣德州人。

translations.literal: Lu Xiaojian was a native of Xuande Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xiaojian came from Xuande Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登天眷二年第，調憲州軍事判官，補尚書省令史，累官太原少尹。

translations.literal: He passed the second-year Tianhui examination, was assigned military judge of Xian Prefecture, supplemented as secretary of the Imperial Secretariat, and rose to vice prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Tianhui examination of year two, served as military judge of Xian Prefecture, became a Secretariat secretary, and rose to vice prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，陝西用兵，尚書省發本路稅粟赴平涼充軍實，期甚嚴迫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading, when Shaanxi was at war, the Imperial Secretariat dispatched that circuit's tax grain to Pingliang for army provisions, with a very strict deadline.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dading, with war in Shaanxi, the Imperial Secretariat sent that circuit's tax grain to Pingliang for the army on a strict deadline.

sentences.zh: 孝儉輒易以金帛，馳至平涼，用省而不失期，並人稱之。

translations.literal: Xiaojian promptly exchanged it for gold and silk, hurried to Pingliang, saved expense without missing the deadline, and the people of Bing praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojian exchanged grain for gold and silk, reached Pingliang in time at lower cost, and was praised throughout Bing.

sentences.zh: 用廉，進官二階，遷同知廣甯尹。

translations.literal: For integrity he was advanced two ranks and transferred to associate prefect of Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: For integrity he was promoted two ranks and made associate prefect of Guangning.

sentences.zh: 廣寧大饑，民多流亡失業，乃借僧粟，留其一歲之用，使平其價市與貧民，既以救民，僧亦獲利。

translations.literal: Guangning suffered great famine; many people fled and lost their livelihoods; he borrowed monks' grain, kept one year's supply, had prices stabilized and sold to the poor; thus the people were saved and the monks also profited.
translations.idiomatic: In great famine at Guangning he borrowed monks' grain, reserved one year's supply, stabilized prices, and sold to the poor—saving the people while the monks also profited.

sentences.zh: 累遷山東東路轉運使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to transport commissioner of the Shandong East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to transport commissioner of the Shandong East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 孝儉素褊躁，與同僚王公謹失歡。

translations.literal: Xiaojian was by nature narrow and irritable and fell out with colleague Wang Gongjin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojian was narrow and irritable and quarreled with colleague Wang Gongjin.

sentences.zh: 其子嘗私用官帑，孝儉不知也。

translations.literal: His son once privately used the official treasury without Xiaojian's knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: His son once used the official treasury without Xiaojian's knowledge.

sentences.zh: 既而改河北西路轉運使，公謹乃發其事。

translations.literal: When he was transferred to transport commissioner of the Hebei West Circuit, Gongjin then exposed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When he became Hebei West transport commissioner, Gongjin exposed the affair.

sentences.zh: 孝儉聞被逮，莫測所以，行至章丘，自縊死。

translations.literal: When Xiaojian heard he was to be arrested he could not fathom why; reaching Zhangqiu he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing he was to be arrested, Xiaojian could not understand why; reaching Zhangqiu he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 十一月，夏人掠鎮戎，陷涇、邠，遂圍平涼。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Xia raided Zhenrong, took Jing and Bin, and then besieged Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Xia raided Zhenrong, took Jing and Bin, and besieged Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 庸矢盡，募人取夏兵射城上箭以濟急用，出府庫賞有功者，人樂為死，平涼賴以完。

translations.literal: Yong's arrows were exhausted; he recruited men to collect arrows the Xia shot onto the walls for urgent use, opened the treasury to reward those with merit, and men gladly died fighting; Pingliang was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Yong's arrows ran out; he recruited men to collect Xia arrows shot onto the walls, rewarded the meritorious from the treasury, and men fought willingly—Pingliang was saved.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，庸移書陝西行省僕散端，大概謂慶陽、平涼、德順陝西重地，長安以西邠為厄塞，當重兵屯守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, Yong wrote to Shaanxi Branch Secretariat Puxian Duan, stating in general that Qingyang, Pingliang, and Deshun were vital places in Shaanxi, and that west of Chang'an, Bin was the strategic chokepoint and should be garrisoned with heavy troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou, Yong wrote to Shaanxi Branch Secretariat Puxian Duan urging heavy garrisons at Qingyang, Pingliang, Deshun, and Bin—the strategic pass west of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 詔賞平涼功，庸進官四階，遷按察轉運使。

translations.literal: An edict rewarded the Pingliang achievement; Yong was advanced four ranks and transferred to surveillance and transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rewarded the Pingliang defense; Yong was promoted four ranks and made surveillance and transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔諸道按察司講究防秋，庸陳便宜曰：「自毾延至積石，雖多溝阪，無長河大山為之遮罩，恃弓箭手以禦侮，其人皆剛猛善鬥，熟于地利，夏人畏之。

translations.literal: In the third year an edict ordered surveillance commissions on all circuits to study autumn defense; Yong set forth expedient measures: "From Duoyan to Jishi, though there are many ravines and hills, there are no great rivers or mountains to screen them; they rely on archers to repel insult; these men are all fierce and skilled in fighting, familiar with the terrain, and the Xia fear them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year circuits were ordered to study autumn defense; Yong argued that from Duoyan to Jishi, lacking great rivers or mountains, the frontier relied on fierce local archers whom the Xia feared.

sentences.zh: 向者徙屯他所，夏人即時犯邊，此近年深患也。

translations.literal: Formerly when garrisons were moved elsewhere, the Xia at once raided the border—this has been a grave affliction in recent years.
translations.idiomatic: When garrisons were moved elsewhere, the Xia immediately raided—the grave affliction of recent years.

sentences.zh: 人情樂土，且耕且戰，緩急將自奮。」

translations.literal: People's feelings cling to their land; farming and fighting together, in urgency they will exert themselves."
translations.idiomatic: People love their native soil; farming and fighting together, they will fight fiercely in crisis.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「防秋之際，宜先清野。」

translations.literal: He also said: "At the season of autumn defense, the countryside should first be cleared."
translations.idiomatic: He also said that before autumn defense the countryside should be cleared.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「掌軍之官不宜臨時易代，兵家所忌，將非其人，屢代何益？」

translations.literal: He also said: "Officers in command of troops should not be changed at the last moment—this is what military strategists forbid; if the general is not the right man, what use is frequent replacement?"
translations.idiomatic: He also said commanders should not be changed at the last moment—a military taboo—and that frequent replacement without the right man was useless.

sentences.zh: 無何，有言庸老不勝任者，即罷之。

translations.literal: Before long someone said Yong was old and unfit for duty, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon someone said Yong was too old for duty and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改定海軍節度使，山東亂，不能赴，按察司劾之，當奪兩官，審理官直之。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to military commissioner of Dinghai Army; Shandong was in turmoil and he could not go; the surveillance commission impeached him and he should have been stripped of two ranks, but the reviewing official vindicated him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon appointed military commissioner of Dinghai Army, he could not go because Shandong was in turmoil; impeached and liable to lose two ranks, a reviewing official vindicated him.

sentences.zh: 庸以病請求醫藥，遂致仕。

translations.literal: Yong requested medicine on grounds of illness and then retired.
translations.idiomatic: Yong requested medicine for illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 興定三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xingding he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xingding he died.

sentences.zh: 李偲，字子友，定州安喜人。

translations.literal: Li Cai, courtesy name Ziyou, was a native of Anxi in Ding Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cai, styled Ziyou, came from Anxi in Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 中天眷二年進士，調遼山簿，累官戶部主事。

translations.literal: He passed the Tianhui second-year jinshi examination, was assigned recorder of Liaoshan, and rose to chief clerk of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Tianhui year-two jinshi examination, served as recorder of Liaoshan, and rose to chief clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起復舊職，除同知河東南路轉運使事。

translations.literal: When his mother's mourning ended he returned to his former post and was appointed associate transport commissioner of the Hedong South Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he returned and was appointed associate transport commissioner of the Hedong South Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大定初，改同知中都路都轉運使事。

translations.literal: In the early Dading period he was changed to associate chief transport commissioner of the Central Capital Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dading he became associate chief transport commissioner of the Central Capital Circuit.

sentences.zh: 僕散忠義行省事於汴京，奏偲幕府，世宗曰：「李偲方治京畿漕事，行省可他選也。」

translations.literal: Puxian Zhongyi, conducting branch secretariat affairs at Bianjing, memorialized Cai for his staff; Emperor Shizong said, "Li Cai is just managing metropolitan transport affairs; the branch secretariat can choose someone else."
translations.idiomatic: Puxian Zhongyi at Bianjing sought Cai for his staff; the emperor said, "Li Cai is managing metropolitan transport—the branch secretariat can choose elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 三年，權知登聞檢院，再遷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year he acted as director of the Petition Office and was again promoted to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he acted as director of the Petition Office and was promoted to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「戶部財用出入，朕難其人。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Revenue disbursements and receipts—I find the right man difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "For revenue receipts and disbursements I find the right man hard to choose.

sentences.zh: 卿非舊勞，資敘尚淺，勿以秩滿例升三品，因循歲月，若不自勉，必不汝貸。」

translations.literal: You are not one of old merit; your qualifications and seniority are still shallow. Do not expect routine promotion to the third rank when your term is fulfilled. Drift along month after month without exerting yourself, and I will certainly not spare you."
translations.idiomatic: You lack long-standing service, and your rank and seniority are still modest. Do not expect an automatic promotion to third rank when your term ends. Drift along without striving, and I will show you no leniency."

sentences.zh: 偲每朝會與高德基屏人私語。

translations.literal: At every court assembly Si would withdraw with Gao Deji for private conversation.
translations.idiomatic: At every court session, Si would take Gao Deji aside for private talks.

sentences.zh: 上聞而怪之，問右丞石琚曰：「李偲果何如人？」

translations.literal: The emperor heard of this and found it strange, and asked the Right Deputy Minister Shi Ju, "What sort of man is Li Si after all?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this, thought it odd, and asked the Right Deputy Minister Shi Ju, "What kind of man is Li Si, really?"

sentences.zh: 琚曰：「亦幹事吏耳。」

translations.literal: Ju said, "He is also merely a capable administrative officer."
translations.idiomatic: Ju replied, "He is just another competent clerk."

sentences.zh: 改同知北京留守、沂州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Co-Commissioner of the Beijing Garrison Command and Military Commissioner of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Si was reassigned as deputy commissioner of the Beijing garrison and military commissioner of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 沂南邊郡，戶部符借民閒田，種禾取槁秸，備警急用度。

translations.literal: Yizhou was a southern border prefecture. The Ministry of Revenue issued an order to borrow idle private fields, plant grain, and take the straw to prepare for emergency expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhou lay on the southern frontier. The Ministry of Revenue ordered that idle private fields be borrowed to grow grain and harvest straw for use in emergencies.

sentences.zh: 偲曰：「如此則農民失業。」

translations.literal: Si said, "If it is done thus, the peasants will lose their livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: Si said, "That would ruin the farmers' livelihoods."

sentences.zh: 具奏止之。

translations.literal: He submitted a full memorial to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne in detail and had the policy halted.

sentences.zh: 轉運司牒郡輸粟朐山，調急夫數萬人，是時久雨泥濘，挽運不能前進。

translations.literal: The Transport Commission sent a dispatch to the prefecture to ship grain to Qushan, mobilizing tens of thousands of corvée laborers. At that time long rains had turned the roads to mud, and the haulers could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The transport office ordered the prefecture to ship grain to Qushan, conscripting tens of thousands of laborers. Prolonged rain had turned the roads to mud, and the convoys could not move.

sentences.zh: 偲遣吏往朐山刺取其官廩，見儲糧數可支半歲，即具其事牒運司，請緩期，毋自困百姓。

translations.literal: Si sent an official to Qushan to investigate the government granary and found the stored grain could supply half a year. He thereupon reported the facts in a dispatch to the Transport Commission, requesting an extension and asking that the people not be worn down unnecessarily.
translations.idiomatic: Si sent an official to inspect the Qushan granary and found stores sufficient for half a year. He reported this to the transport office and asked for a deadline extension so the people would not be needlessly exhausted.

sentences.zh: 先是，郡縣街陌間聽民作廛舍，取其僦直。

translations.literal: Previously, along the streets and lanes of prefectures and counties, the people had been allowed to build shops and charged rent.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, local governments had allowed people to build shops along city streets and collected rent on them.

sentences.zh: 至是，罷收僦直，廛舍一切撤毀。

translations.literal: At this time rent collection was abolished and all shops were entirely demolished.
translations.idiomatic: Now rent collection was abolished and all the shops were torn down.

sentences.zh: 他郡奉承號令，督百姓必盡撤去，使街陌繩齊矢棘如初時然後止。

translations.literal: Other prefectures, complying with the order, compelled the people to remove everything completely, making the streets and lanes as neat and unobstructed as at the beginning before stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Other prefectures obeyed to the letter, forcing people to tear everything down until the streets were as bare and orderly as before.

sentences.zh: 偲獨教民撤治前卻不齊一者三五所，使巷道端正即已，民便之。

translations.literal: Si alone instructed the people to remove and repair only the three or five places that were not aligned before, straightening the lanes and stopping there, to the people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: Si alone told people to pull down and straighten only the few misaligned spots—three or five of them—and stop once the lanes were tidy, which the people found far more manageable.

sentences.zh: 改陝西西路轉運使，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Transport Commissioner of Shaanxi West Circuit and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed transport commissioner for Shaanxi West Circuit, where he died.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：毛碩、李上達、曹望之、李偲之流，皆金之能吏也。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Mao Shuo, Li Shangda, Cao Wangzhi, Li Si, and men of that sort were all capable officials of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In summary: Mao Shuo, Li Shangda, Cao Wangzhi, Li Si, and their like were all able administrators of the Jin.

sentences.zh: 望之悻悻然以求大用，君子無取焉。

translations.literal: Wangzhi resentfully sought great employment; a gentleman would not approve of this.
translations.idiomatic: Wangzhi pursued high office with thinly veiled resentment—a quality no gentleman would admire.

sentences.zh: 徒單克寧

translations.literal: Tudan Kening
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Kening

sentences.zh: 徒單克寧，本名習顯，其先金源縣人，徙居比古土之地，後徙置猛安于山東，遂占籍萊州。

translations.literal: Tudan Kening, original name Xixian, his ancestors were people of Jinyuan County; they moved to live in the Bigutu region, and later, when a military colony was established in Shandong, they registered domicile in Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tudan Kening, whose original name was Xixian, came from ancestors of Jinyuan County who had moved to the Bigutu region. When a military colony was later established in Shandong, the family registered domicile in Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 父況者，官至汾陽軍節度使。

translations.literal: His father Kuang rose to the post of Military Commissioner of Fenyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuang served as military commissioner of the Fenyang garrison.

sentences.zh: 克寧資質渾厚，寡言笑，善騎射，有勇略，通女直、契丹字。

translations.literal: Kening was of solid character, sparing in speech and laughter, skilled at horsemanship and archery, brave and resourceful, and versed in Jurchen and Khitan script.
translations.idiomatic: Kening was steady and solid by nature, quiet and sparing with laughter, skilled in riding and archery, courageous and shrewd, and literate in Jurchen and Khitan script.

sentences.zh: 左丞相希尹，克寧母舅。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor Xiyin was Kening's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Xiyin was his maternal uncle.

sentences.zh: 熙宗問希尹表戚中誰可侍衛者，希尹奏曰：「習顯可用。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong asked Xiyin who among his maternal relatives could serve in the imperial guard. Xiyin memorialized, "Xixian may be used."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong asked Xiyin which of his maternal kin might serve in the imperial guard. Xiyin answered, "Xixian would serve well."

sentences.zh: 以為符寶祗候。

translations.literal: He was appointed Keeper of Seals and Treasures Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Kening was appointed attendant keeper of the imperial seals and regalia.

sentences.zh: 是時，悼後幹政，後弟裴滿忽土侮克寧，克寧毆之。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Dao governed affairs. The empress dowager's younger brother Peiman Hutu insulted Kening, and Kening beat him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Dowager Dao held power. Her younger brother Peiman Hutu insulted Kening, and Kening struck him.

sentences.zh: 明日，忽土以告悼後，後曰：「習顯剛直，必汝之過也。」

translations.literal: The next day Hutu reported this to Empress Dowager Dao. The empress dowager said, "Xixian is upright and firm; the fault must be yours."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Hutu complained to the empress dowager, who said, "Xixian is blunt and upright—the fault must be yours."

sentences.zh: 已而充護衛，轉符寶郎，遷侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使，改忠順軍節度使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed to the imperial guard, transferred to Seal-and-Treasure Officer, promoted to Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard Horse-and-Foot Army, and reassigned as Military Commissioner of the Zhongshun Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed to the imperial guard, then promoted through posts as seal officer and commander of the palace guard cavalry and infantry, before becoming military commissioner of the Zhongshun Army.

sentences.zh: 克寧娶宗幹女嘉祥縣主，同母兄蒲甲判大宗正事，海陵心忌之，出為西京留守，構致其罪誅之，因降克寧知滕陽軍。

translations.literal: Kening married the daughter of Zonggan, the Princess of Jiaxiang County. His elder half-brother Pujia served as vice-director of the Imperial Clan Court. Emperor Hailing secretly resented this, sent Pujia out as Western Capital Garrison Commissioner, fabricated charges against him and executed him, and accordingly demoted Kening to prefect of Tengyang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Kening married Zonggan's daughter, the Princess of Jiaxiang. His elder half-brother Pujia was vice-director of the Imperial Clan Court. Emperor Hailing, secretly envious, posted Pujia to the western capital, framed him, and had him executed; Kening was demoted to commandant of Tengyang.

sentences.zh: 曆宿州防禦使、胡裏改路節度使、曷懶路兵馬都總管。

translations.literal: He served as Military Commissioner of Suzhou, Military Commissioner of Huligai Circuit, and Grand Commander of the Yilan Circuit military forces.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military commissioner of Suzhou, military commissioner of Huligai Circuit, and grand commander of the Yilan Circuit forces.

sentences.zh: 大定初，詔克寧以本路兵會東京。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dading era, an edict ordered Kening to assemble the troops of his circuit at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dading era, Kening was ordered to muster his circuit's troops at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 遷左翼都統。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Wing Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander of the left wing.

sentences.zh: 詔與廣甯尹僕散渾坦、同知廣甯尹完顏岩雅、肇州防禦使唐括烏也，從右副元帥完顏謀衍討契丹窩斡。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him, together with Guangning Prefect Pusan Hondan, Co-Prefect of Guangning Wanyan Yanya, and Zhaozhou Military Commissioner Tangqut Wuye, to follow the Right Vice Marshal Wanyan Mouyan in campaigning against the Khitan Wohe.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to join Guangning prefect Pusan Hondan, deputy prefect Wanyan Yanya, and Zhaozhou commissioner Tangqut Wuye under Vice Marshal Wanyan Mouyan to suppress the Khitan rebel Wohe.

sentences.zh: 趨濟州。

translations.literal: They hastened toward Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: They pushed toward Jizhou.
