sentences.zh: 謀衍用契丹降吏颭者計策襲賊輜重，克寧與紇石烈志寧為殿，與賊遇於長濼。

translations.literal: Mouyan adopted the plan of the surrendered Khitan officer Zhanzhe to raid the enemy baggage train. Kening and Heshelie Zhining served as rearguard and encountered the enemy at Changliao.
translations.idiomatic: Mouyan followed a plan from the Khitan defector Zhanzhe to strike the rebel supply train. Kening and Heshelie Zhining formed the rearguard and clashed with the enemy at Changliao.

sentences.zh: 謀衍使伏兵於左翼之側。

translations.literal: Mouyan placed ambush troops on the flank of the left wing.
translations.idiomatic: Mouyan hid troops on the left flank.

sentences.zh: 賊二萬餘躡吾後，又以騎四百餘突出左翼伏兵之間，欲繞出陣後攻我。

translations.literal: More than twenty thousand of the enemy pursued them from behind, and more than four hundred cavalry burst out between the left-wing ambush, intending to circle behind the formation and attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Over twenty thousand rebels pressed from the rear while more than four hundred horsemen broke through between the left-flank ambush, trying to circle behind the line and strike.

sentences.zh: 克寧與善射二十餘人拒之。

translations.literal: Kening and more than twenty skilled archers resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: Kening and some twenty crack archers held them off.

sentences.zh: 眾曰：「賊眾我寡，不若與伏兵合擊，或與大軍相依，可以萬全。」

translations.literal: The men said, "The enemy are many and we are few. Better to join the ambush in a combined strike, or stay close to the main army—that would be entirely safe."
translations.idiomatic: His men said, "The enemy outnumber us—we should either link up with the ambush or fall back on the main force. That would be safest."

sentences.zh: 克寧曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Kening said, "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Kening replied, "No.

sentences.zh: 若賊出陣後，則前後夾擊，我敗矣，大軍不可俟也。」

translations.literal: If the enemy get behind the formation, they will strike them from front and rear and they will be defeated. The main army cannot be waited for."
translations.idiomatic: If they get behind us, we will be crushed between two fires. We cannot wait for the main army."

sentences.zh: 於是奮擊，賊乃卻。

translations.literal: Thereupon he fought hard, and the enemy then retreated.
translations.idiomatic: He charged hard, and the enemy fell back.

sentences.zh: 左翼萬戶襄與大軍合擊之，賊遂敗，追奔十餘裏，二年四月一日也。

translations.literal: Left Wing Myriarch Xiang and the main army combined to strike them; the enemy were defeated and pursued for more than ten li. It was the first day of the fourth month of the second year.
translations.idiomatic: Myriarch Xiang of the left wing and the main force closed in together, routing the enemy and chasing them more than ten li. This was the first day of the fourth month of year two.

sentences.zh: 越九日，複追及賊於霿𩃭河。

translations.literal: Nine days later they again caught up with the enemy at the Menglong River.
translations.idiomatic: Nine days later they caught the rebels again at the Menglong River.

sentences.zh: 左翼軍先與賊戰，克寧以騎二千追掩十五裏，賊迫澗不得亟渡，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: The left-wing army first engaged the enemy. Kening with two thousand cavalry pursued and enveloped them for fifteen li. The enemy, pressed against a ravine, could not quickly cross, and casualties were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: The left wing met the enemy first. Kening raced fifteen li with two thousand horsemen and pinned them against a ravine they could not cross quickly, inflicting heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 賊收軍返旆，大軍尚未至，克寧令軍士下馬射賊，賊遂引而南。

translations.literal: The enemy gathered their forces and turned back. The main army had not yet arrived. Kening ordered the soldiers to dismount and shoot at the enemy, and the enemy then withdrew southward.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels regrouped and turned back before the main army arrived. Kening had his men dismount and shoot, driving the enemy south.

sentences.zh: 是時，窩斡已再北，元帥謀衍利鹵掠，駐師白濼。

translations.literal: At that time Wohe had already moved north again. Marshal Mouyan, coveting plunder, halted the army at Bailiao.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wohe had retreated north again. Marshal Mouyan, intent on loot, camped at Bailiao.

sentences.zh: 世宗訝其持久，遣問之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong wondered at the prolonged delay and sent someone to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong was surprised by the delay and sent an envoy to ask why.

sentences.zh: 謀衍曰：「賊騎壯，我騎弱，此少駐所以完養馬力也。

translations.literal: Mouyan said, "The enemy's cavalry are strong and ours are weak. This brief halt is to restore and nurture the horses' strength.
translations.idiomatic: Mouyan replied, "Their horses are strong and ours are weak. We are pausing here to rest the mounts.

sentences.zh: 不然，非益萬騎不可勝。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, without adding ten thousand cavalry, they cannot be defeated."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise we would need ten thousand more horsemen before we could win."

sentences.zh: 克寧奮然而言曰：「吾馬固不少，但帥不得人耳。

translations.literal: Kening spoke up heatedly, "Our horses are indeed not few, but the commander is not the right man.
translations.idiomatic: Kening spoke up angrily, "We have plenty of horses—the problem is we do not have the right commander.

sentences.zh: 其意常利虜掠，賊至則引避，賊去則緩隨之，故賊常得善牧，而我常拾其蹂踐之餘，此吾馬所以弱也。

translations.literal: His mind is always bent on loot. When the enemy arrive he withdraws and avoids them; when they leave he follows slowly. Thus the enemy always get good pasture, while they constantly gather what remains after their trampling—this is why their horses are weak.
translations.idiomatic: He is always looking for loot. When the enemy appear he pulls back; when they leave he trails far behind. The rebels always find good pasture while they are left with what has been trampled bare—that is why their horses are weak.

sentences.zh: 今誠能更置良帥，雖不益兵，可以有功。

translations.literal: If they can truly replace him with a good commander, even without adding troops, merit can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Replace him with a capable commander and they can win even without reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 不然，騎雖十倍，未見其利也。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, even if cavalry were increased tenfold, he does not see the advantage."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise ten times the cavalry would still do them little good."

sentences.zh: 朝廷知其議，召還謀衍，以平章政事僕散忠義兼右副元帥。

translations.literal: The court learned of his opinion, recalled Mouyan, and appointed Pusan Zhongyi, Grand Councilor, concurrently as Right Vice Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the court heard this, Mouyan was recalled and Grand Councilor Pusan Zhongyi was named vice marshal in his place.

sentences.zh: 師將發，賊聲言乞降。

translations.literal: As the army was about to march, the enemy publicly claimed they wished to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the army was about to move out, the rebels announced they wanted to surrender.

sentences.zh: 克寧曰：「賊初困蹙，且無降意，所以揚言者，是欲緩吾師期也。

translations.literal: Kening said, "The enemy were at first hard pressed and had no intent to surrender. Their public announcement is meant to delay our army's schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Kening said, "They were cornered and had no real wish to surrender. This talk is meant to stall our advance.

sentences.zh: 不若攻其未備，賊若挫衄，則其降必速。

translations.literal: Better to attack them while they are unprepared. If the enemy suffer defeat, their surrender will certainly come quickly.
translations.idiomatic: Better to strike before they are ready. Beat them once and they will surrender in earnest.

sentences.zh: 如其不降，乘其怠而急擊之，可一戰而定也。」

translations.literal: If they do not surrender, seize their slackness and strike urgently—a single battle can settle it."
translations.idiomatic: If they still refuse, hit them hard while they are off guard and the matter can be settled in one fight."

sentences.zh: 忠義以為然，乃與克寧出中路，遂敗賊兵于羅不魯之地。

translations.literal: Zhongyi agreed, and together with Kening advanced by the central route, defeating the enemy at Luobulu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyi agreed, marched the center route with Kening, and routed the rebels at Luobulu.

sentences.zh: 賊奔七渡河，負險為柵，克寧覘知賊柵之背其勢可上，乃潛師夜登，俯射之，大軍自下攻，賊潰，皆遁去。

translations.literal: The enemy fled to Qiduh River, relying on the terrain to build palisades. Kening reconnoitered and learned that behind the enemy palisade the ground could be ascended. He secretly moved troops up by night, shot down from above, while the main army attacked from below. The enemy collapsed and all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to the Seven Crossings River and fortified a defile. Kening found a path up the slope behind their stockade, sent men up by night to shoot down while the main force attacked from below. The rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 契丹平，克寧除太原尹。

translations.literal: When the Khitan rebellion was pacified, Kening was appointed Prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After the Khitan rising was suppressed, Kening was made prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 未閱月，宋吳璘侵陝右，元帥左都監徒單合喜乞益兵，遣克寧佩金牌，駐軍平涼。

translations.literal: Within less than a month, Wu Lin of Song invaded western Shaanxi. Marshal Left Overseer Tushi Hexi requested reinforcements. Kening was sent bearing the golden tally and stationed his army at Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Less than a month later, Song general Wu Lin invaded western Shaanxi. Marshal Tushi Hexi asked for reinforcements, and Kening was dispatched with an imperial gold tally to camp at Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 詔合喜曰：「朕遣克寧參議軍事，此其智勇足敵萬人，不必益軍也。」

translations.literal: An edict told Hexi, "I am sending Kening to counsel on military affairs. His wisdom and courage are the equal of ten thousand men—there is no need to add troops."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Hexi, "I am sending Kening to advise you. One man of his wit and courage is worth ten thousand—you need no more troops."

sentences.zh: 克寧至，下令安輯，未幾，民皆完聚。

translations.literal: When Kening arrived, he issued orders to pacify and organize the people. Before long, the populace had all been restored and reassembled.
translations.idiomatic: Kening arrived, issued orders to pacify the region, and soon the people were settled and restored.

sentences.zh: 治兵伐宋，右丞相僕散忠義駐南京節制諸軍，左副元帥紇石烈志寧經略邊事，克寧改益都尹，兼山東路兵馬都總管、行軍都統。

translations.literal: While organizing troops to campaign against Song, Right Chancellor Pusan Zhongyi was stationed at the Southern Capital to command all armies; Left Vice Marshal Heshelie Zhining managed frontier affairs. Kening was reassigned as Prefect of Yidu, concurrently Grand Commander of Shandong Circuit's military forces and Campaign Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: As forces were marshaled against Song, Right Chancellor Pusan Zhongyi took command at the Southern Capital while Left Vice Marshal Heshelie Zhining managed the frontier. Kening became prefect of Yidu and grand commander of Shandong's forces and the field army.

sentences.zh: 四年，元帥府欲遣左都監璋以兵四千由水路進，詔曰：「可付都統徒單習顯，仍益兵二千，擇良將副之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Marshal's Headquarters wished to send Left Overseer Zhang with four thousand troops by water route. An edict said, "This may be entrusted to Campaign Commander Tushi Xixian, with two thousand more troops added and a good general chosen as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In year four the marshal's headquarters planned to send Left Overseer Zhang with four thousand men by river. The court ordered, "Give the command to Commander Tushi Xixian instead, add two thousand troops, and assign a capable deputy.

sentences.zh: 璋可經略山東。」

translations.literal: Zhang may oversee Shandong."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang may take charge of Shandong instead."

sentences.zh: 於是，克寧出軍楚、泗之間，與宋將魏勝相拒于楚州之十八裏口。

translations.literal: Thereupon Kening led his army out between Chu and Si, confronting Song general Wei Sheng at the Eighteen-Li Pass of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kening marched between Chu and Si and faced Song general Wei Sheng at the Eighteen-Li Pass outside Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏勝取弊舟鑿其底，貫以大木，列植水中，別以船載巨石貫以鐵鎖，沉之水底，以塞十八裏口及淮渡舟路。

translations.literal: Wei Sheng took broken boats, bored holes in their bottoms, ran large timbers through them, and planted them in the water in rows. Separately he loaded ships with huge stones bound by iron chains and sank them to the bottom to block the Eighteen-Li Pass and the river crossing at the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Sheng took old boats, drilled their hulls, threaded them with great timbers, and planted them in rows across the water. Other boats loaded with boulders were chained and sunk to block the pass and the Huai crossing.

sentences.zh: 以步兵四萬人屯于淮渡南岸、運河之間。

translations.literal: He stationed forty thousand infantry between the south bank of the Huai crossing and the canal.
translations.idiomatic: He posted forty thousand infantry between the south bank of the Huai ford and the canal.

sentences.zh: 克寧使斜卯和尚選善游者沒水，系大繩植木上，數百人於岸上引繩曳一植木，皆拔出之，徹去沉船。

translations.literal: Kening had Xiemao Heshang select skilled swimmers to dive underwater, tie great ropes to the planted timbers, and have several hundred men on shore pull the ropes and drag out each planted timber one by one, all being pulled up and the sunken ships removed.
translations.idiomatic: Kening had Xiemao Heshang pick strong swimmers to dive beneath the obstacles, lash ropes to the planted timbers, and haul each one out with hundreds of men on shore until the sunken blockships were cleared.

sentences.zh: 進至淮口，宋兵來拒，隔水矢石俱發。

translations.literal: Advancing to the mouth of the Huai, Song troops came to resist; across the water arrows and stones flew together.
translations.idiomatic: At the Huai mouth Song troops blocked their way, hurling arrows and stones across the water.

sentences.zh: 斜卯和尚以竹編籬捍矢石，複拔去植木沉船，師遂入淮。

translations.literal: Xiemao Heshang used bamboo-woven screens to ward off arrows and stones, again pulled out the planted timbers and sunken ships, and the army then entered the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Xiemao Heshang shielded the work with woven bamboo screens, cleared the obstacles again, and the army entered the Huai.

sentences.zh: 與宋兵奪渡口，合戰數四，猛安長壽先行薄岸，水淺，先率勁卒數人涉水登岸，敗其津口兵五百人，餘眾皆濟。

translations.literal: Contending with Song troops for the crossing, they joined battle repeatedly. Military Administrator Changshou advanced first close to the shore. The water was shallow; he first led several elite soldiers wading ashore, defeated five hundred of their ferry-guard troops, and the rest of the force all crossed.
translations.idiomatic: They fought repeatedly for the crossing. Military Administrator Changshou led the way in shallow water with a handful of picked men, routed five hundred Song troops at the ferry, and the rest of the army followed across.

sentences.zh: 宋兵四百餘自清河口來，鎮國上將軍蒲察阿離合懣以步兵百人禦之。

translations.literal: More than four hundred Song troops came from Qinghe Mouth. Zhenguo Upper General Pucha Alihemao with one hundred infantry opposed them.
translations.idiomatic: Over four hundred Song soldiers approached from Qinghe Mouth. Zhenguo Upper General Pucha Alihemao met them with a hundred infantrymen.

sentences.zh: 克寧自與紮也銀術可五騎先行六七裏與戰，銀術可先登，奮擊敗之。

translations.literal: Kening himself with Zhaye Yinshuhe and five horsemen rode ahead six or seven li to fight. Yinshuhe mounted first, fought hard, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Kening himself rode ahead with Zhaye Yinshuhe and three other horsemen for six or seven li to meet them. Yinshuhe charged first and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 宋大兵整陣來拒，克寧麾兵前戰，自旦至午，宋兵敗，逾運河為陣，餘眾數千皆走入營中。

translations.literal: A large Song army formed ranks to resist. Kening commanded his troops forward to battle from dawn until noon. The Song army was defeated, crossed the canal to form a new formation, and several thousand survivors all fled into their camp.
translations.idiomatic: A large Song force formed up to block them. Kening attacked from dawn till noon, broke the Song line, and chased several thousand survivors back across the canal into their camp.

sentences.zh: 克寧使以火箭射其營舍，盡焚，逾河撤橋，與其大軍相會。

translations.literal: Kening had fire arrows shot at their camp buildings and burned them all. Crossing the river he removed the bridges and joined his main army.
translations.idiomatic: Kening fired flaming arrows into the camp and burned it out, then crossed the river, destroyed the bridges, and rejoined the main force.

sentences.zh: 隔水射之，宋兵不能為陣。

translations.literal: Shooting across the water at them, the Song troops could not form ranks.
translations.idiomatic: They rained arrows across the water until the Song troops could no longer hold formation.

sentences.zh: 猛安鈔兀以六十騎擊宋騎兵千餘，不利，少卻。

translations.literal: Military Administrator Chaowu with sixty cavalry attacked more than a thousand Song cavalry, fared poorly, and withdrew slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Military Administrator Chaowu charged a thousand Song horsemen with sixty riders, got the worse of it, and fell back slightly.

sentences.zh: 克寧以猛安賽剌九十騎橫擊之，宋兵大敗。

translations.literal: Kening sent Military Administrator Saila with ninety cavalry to strike them crosswise, and the Song army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Kening sent Military Administrator Saila with ninety horsemen in a flanking charge, and the Song force was routed.

sentences.zh: 追至楚州，射殺魏勝，遂取楚州及淮陰縣。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Chuzhou, they shot and killed Wei Sheng, and then took Chuzhou and Huaiyin County.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued to Chuzhou, killed Wei Sheng with an arrow, and captured Chuzhou and Huaiyin County.

sentences.zh: 是役也，賽剌功居多。

translations.literal: In this campaign, Saila's merit was the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle Saila deserved the greatest credit.

sentences.zh: 是時，宋屢遣使請和，僕散忠義、紇石烈志寧約以世為叔侄國，割還海、泗、唐、鄧四州。

translations.literal: At that time Song repeatedly sent envoys seeking peace. Pusan Zhongyi and Heshelie Zhining agreed that the two states would be uncle and nephew in perpetuity and that Hai, Si, Tang, and Deng—four prefectures—would be ceded back.
translations.idiomatic: Song had repeatedly sued for peace. Pusan Zhongyi and Heshelie Zhining agreed to a permanent uncle-nephew relationship between the states and the return of Hai, Si, Tang, and Deng.

sentences.zh: 宋人尚遷延有請，及克寧取楚州，宋人乃大懼，一一如約。

translations.literal: The Song people still delayed and made requests. When Kening took Chuzhou, the Song were greatly afraid and complied with everything exactly as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The Song had still been stalling and bargaining until Kening captured Chuzhou; then they were thoroughly alarmed and agreed to every term.

sentences.zh: 兵罷，改大名尹，曆河間、東平尹，召為都點檢。

translations.literal: When the campaign ended, he was reassigned as Prefect of Daming, then served as Prefect of Hejian and Dongping, and was summoned as Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After the war he became prefect of Daming, then served at Hejian and Dongping before being recalled as grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從丞相志寧北伐，還師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed Chancellor Zhining on the northern campaign and returned with the army.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he joined Chancellor Zhining's northern expedition and returned with the army.

sentences.zh: 十一月皇太子生日，世宗置酒東宮，賜克寧金帶。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the crown prince's birthday, Shizong held a banquet in the Eastern Palace and bestowed on Kening a golden belt.
translations.idiomatic: That November, on the crown prince's birthday, Emperor Shizong held a feast in the Eastern Palace and gave Kening a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷樞密副使，兼知大興府事，改太子太保，樞密副使如故。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council, concurrently administering affairs of Daxing Prefecture, and changed to Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince while retaining his post as Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he became vice commissioner of the privy council and prefect of Daxing, was made grand preceptor of the crown prince, and kept his privy council post.

sentences.zh: 拜平章政事，封密國公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Miguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Mi.

sentences.zh: 克寧女嫁為沈王永成妃，得罪，克寧不悅，求致仕，不許，罷為東京留守。

translations.literal: Kening's daughter, who had married as consort to Prince Yong of Shen, Yongcheng, offended and displeased Kening. He requested retirement but was not permitted; instead he was dismissed to serve as Eastern Capital Garrison Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Kening's daughter, married to Prince Yong of Shen, gave offense. Unhappy, Kening asked to retire but was refused and instead demoted to eastern capital garrison commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，上將複相克寧，改南京留守，兼河南統軍使。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor wished to restore him as chancellor; he was changed to Southern Capital Garrison Commissioner, concurrently Commander-in-Chief of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor planned to restore him as chancellor. He was posted as southern capital garrison commissioner and commander-in-chief of Henan.

sentences.zh: 遣使者諭之曰：「統軍使未嘗以留守兼之，此朕意也。

translations.literal: An envoy was sent to instruct him, "The post of Commander-in-Chief has never been held concurrently with Garrison Commissioner—this is my intention.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy told him, "No one has ever held the garrison and the frontier command together—that is deliberate on my part.

sentences.zh: 可過京師入見。」

translations.literal: You may pass through the capital to have an audience."
translations.idiomatic: Come through the capital for an audience on your way."

sentences.zh: 克寧至京師，複拜平章政事，授世襲不紮土河猛安兼親管謀克。

translations.literal: When Kening reached the capital, he was again appointed Grand Councilor and granted the hereditary Military Colony of Buzhatuhe with personally supervised military households.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital Kening was again made grand councilor and granted the hereditary military colony of Buzhatuhe with direct command of its military households.

sentences.zh: 世宗欲以制書親授克寧，主者不知上意，及克寧已受制，上謂克寧曰：「此制朕欲親授與卿，誤授之於外也。」

translations.literal: Shizong wished to hand the imperial patent to Kening in person. The official in charge did not know the emperor's intent, and by the time Kening had already received the patent, the emperor said to Kening, "I intended to grant this patent to you personally; it was mistakenly given to you outside."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong had meant to present the patent personally, but the protocol officer did not know. After Kening had already received it, the emperor said, "I meant to give you this patent myself—it was handed to you outside by mistake."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「朕欲盡徙卿宗族在山東者居之近地，卿族多，官田少，無以盡給之。」

translations.literal: He also said, "I wish to move all your clan in Shandong to settle near you, but your clan is large and official fields are few—I cannot fully provide for them all."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "I wanted to resettle all your kin from Shandong nearby, but your clan is large and there is not enough official land to go around."

sentences.zh: 乃選其最親者徙之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he selected those closest to him and moved them.
translations.idiomatic: So he moved only his closest relatives.

sentences.zh: 十九年，拜右丞相，徙封譚國公。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Right Chancellor and transferred in enfeoffment to Duke of Tanguo.
translations.idiomatic: In year nineteen he became right chancellor and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Tan.

sentences.zh: 克寧辭曰：「臣無功，不明國家大事，更內外重任，當自愧。

translations.literal: Kening declined, saying, "Your servant has no merit and does not understand the great affairs of state. To receive further weighty duties at home and abroad—I ought to feel ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Kening declined, saying, "I have achieved nothing and do not grasp the weightiest affairs of state. To take on such responsibilities again, inward and outward—I should be ashamed.

sentences.zh: 乞歸田裏，以盡餘年。」

translations.literal: He requested to return to his fields and village to spend his remaining years."
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire to the countryside for his remaining years."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕念眾人之功無出卿右者，卿慎重得大臣體，毋複多讓。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I consider that among all men's achievements none surpass yours; you are careful and possess the bearing of a great minister—do not decline further."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "No one's service surpasses yours; you have the bearing of a great minister—do not decline again."

sentences.zh: 克寧出朝，上使徒單懷忠諭之曰：「凡人醉時醒時處事不同，卿今日親賓慶會，可一飲，過今日可勿飲也。」

translations.literal: When Kening left court, the emperor sent Tudan Huaizhong to instruct him: "When people are drunk or sober they handle affairs differently; today you have a celebration with kin and guests—you may drink once; after today do not drink again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Tudan Huaizhong to tell him: "You may drink once at today's family celebration; after that, drink no more."

sentences.zh: 克寧頓首謝曰：「陛下念臣及此，臣之福也。」

translations.literal: Kening bowed his head and thanked him, saying, "That Your Majesty thinks of your servant thus is your servant's good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Kening bowed and said, "Your Majesty's care for me is my good fortune."

sentences.zh: 克寧為相，持正守大體，至於簿書期會，不屑屑然也。

translations.literal: As chancellor, Kening upheld rectitude and guarded the great principles; as for ledgers and scheduled meetings, he was not finicky about them.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor Kening upheld principle and the larger frame; he cared little for routine paperwork and schedules.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘗曰：「習顯在樞密，未嘗有過舉。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong once said, "When Xixian was in the Privy Council he never once made a mistaken act."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong said, "Xixian never once erred in the Privy Council."

sentences.zh: 謂克寧曰：「宰相之職，進賢為上。」

translations.literal: He said to Kening, "The chancellor's duty is to advance the worthy above all."
translations.idiomatic: He told Kening, "A chancellor's first duty is to advance worthy men."

sentences.zh: 克寧謝曰：「臣愚幸得備位宰輔，但不能明於知人，以此為恨耳。」

translations.literal: Kening thanked him and said, "Your foolish servant is fortunate to hold a place among the chief ministers, but I am not clear-sighted in knowing men—this is my regret."
translations.idiomatic: Kening replied, "I am fortunate to serve as chancellor, but I am poor at judging men—that is my regret."

sentences.zh: 二十一年，左丞相守道為尚書令，克寧為左丞相，徙封定國公，懇求致仕。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Left Chancellor Shoudao became Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Kening became Left Chancellor; he was transferred in enfeoffment to Duke of Dingguo and earnestly requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-one Shoudao became Director of the Imperial Secretariat and Kening left chancellor, was re-enfeoffed Duke of Ding, and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「汝立功立事，乃登相位，朝廷是賴，年雖及，未可去也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You established merit and affairs and thus rose to the chancellorship; the court relies on you; though your years are advanced, you cannot yet leave."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You earned your place at court; we still need you—you cannot leave yet."

sentences.zh: 後三日，與守道奏事，俱跪而請曰：「臣等齒發皆衰，幸陛下賜以餘年。」

translations.literal: Three days later, together with Shoudao he memorialized on affairs, both kneeling to request: "Our teeth and hair are both decayed; we beg Your Majesty to grant us remaining years."
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he and Shoudao knelt and asked, "We are old; grant us our remaining years."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「上相坐而論道，不惟其官惟其人，豈可屢改易之邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The chief minister sits and discusses the Way—it is not the office but the man; how can he be changed repeatedly?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The chief minister discusses policy by virtue of the man, not the title—he must not be changed lightly."

sentences.zh: 頃之，克寧改樞密使，而難其代。

translations.literal: Before long Kening was changed to Privy Council Commissioner, and a successor was hard to find.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Kening became privy council commissioner, and no easy replacement was found.

sentences.zh: 複以守道為左丞相，虛尚書令位者數年，其重如此。

translations.literal: Shoudao was again made Left Chancellor, and the post of Director of the Imperial Secretariat was left vacant for several years—such was the weight attached to it.
translations.idiomatic: Shoudao returned as left chancellor while the director's post stayed vacant for years—such was Kening's importance.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以司徒兼樞密使。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand Preceptor concurrently Privy Council Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand preceptor and privy council commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，詔賜今名。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year an edict granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two an edict gave him his present name Tudan.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，克寧複以年老為請。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year Kening again requested on grounds of age.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three he again asked to retire on account of age.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿昔在政府，勤勞夙夜，除卿樞密使亦可以優逸矣。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "You formerly in government toiled early and late; appointing you Privy Council Commissioner can also allow ease.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "You toiled long in government; as privy commissioner you may have some ease.

sentences.zh: 朕念舊臣無幾人，萬一邊隅有警，選將帥，授方略，山川險要，兵道軍謀，舍卿誰可與共者？

translations.literal: I think of old ministers—there are few left; if perchance the border has an alarm, in choosing generals, conferring strategy, knowing mountains and passes, military routes and plans—apart from you, with whom can I share this?
translations.idiomatic: Few old ministers remain; if the frontier alarms, who but you can choose generals, set strategy, and know the passes and routes of war?

sentences.zh: 勉為朕留！」

translations.literal: Strive to remain for me!"
translations.idiomatic: Stay on for my sake!"

sentences.zh: 克寧乃不敢複言。

translations.literal: Kening then dared not speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Kening said no more.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，世宗幸上京，皇太子守國，詔左丞相守道與克寧俱留中都輔太子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Emperor Shizong visited the Upper Capital; the crown prince guarded the state; an edict ordered Left Chancellor Shoudao and Kening both to remain at the Central Capital to assist the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four the emperor went to the Upper Capital; Shoudao and Kening were left at the Central Capital to assist the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 上謂克寧曰：「朕巡省之後，萬一有事，卿必躬親之，毋忽細微，圖難於其易可也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to Kening, "After my tour, if anything arises you must handle it in person; do not neglect the small; plan for difficulty while it is still easy."
translations.idiomatic: He told Kening, "If anything arises while I am away, handle it yourself; neglect no detail; solve easy problems before they grow hard."

sentences.zh: 二十五年，左丞相守道賜宴北部，詔克寧行左丞相事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Left Chancellor Shoudao was given a banquet in the northern quarter; an edict ordered Kening to act as Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-five Shoudao feasted in the north; Kening was ordered to act as left chancellor.

sentences.zh: 九月，世宗還京師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Emperor Shizong returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十一月，克寧表請立金源郡王為皇太孫，以系天下之望。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Kening memorialized requesting that Prince Jinyuan be established as imperial great-grandson to fix the world's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he memorialized to establish Prince Jinyuan as imperial great-grandson and fix the succession.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：「今宣孝皇太子陵寢已畢，東宮虛位，此社稷安危之事，陛下明聖超越前古，寧不察此。

translations.literal: The gist was: "Now the tomb of the late Xuanxiao crown prince is completed and the Eastern Palace stands empty—this is a matter of the altars' safety and peril; Your Majesty is enlightened beyond the ancients—would you not observe this?
translations.idiomatic: He wrote that with the crown prince's tomb complete and the Eastern Palace empty, the succession was a matter of dynastic safety, which the emperor must not ignore.

sentences.zh: 事貴果斷，不可緩也。

translations.literal: In affairs decisiveness is valued; it cannot be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: The matter required swift decision, not delay.

sentences.zh: 緩之則起覬覦之心，來讒佞之言。

translations.literal: Delay will breed covetous hearts and bring slanderous words.
translations.idiomatic: Delay would breed ambition and slander.

sentences.zh: 讒佞之言起，雖欲無疑得乎？

translations.literal: When slanderous words arise, even if one wishes to be without doubt, can one?
translations.idiomatic: Once slander begins, doubt cannot be avoided.

sentences.zh: 茲事深可畏、大可慎，而不畏不慎，豈惟儲位久虛，而骨肉之禍，自此始矣。

translations.literal: This matter is deeply to be feared and greatly to be cautioned; if one does not fear and caution, not only will the heir's place long stand empty, but calamity among kin will begin from this.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was deeply dangerous: without caution, not only would the heir's place stay empty, but kin would begin to destroy one another.

sentences.zh: 臣愚不避危身之罪，伏願亟立嫡孫金源郡王為皇太孫，以釋天下之惑，塞覬覦之端，絕構禍之萌，則宗廟獲安，臣民蒙福。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant does not avoid the crime of endangering his person; I prostrate myself hoping you will quickly establish the legitimate grandson Prince Jinyuan as imperial great-grandson, to release the world's doubts, block the path of covetousness, cut off the sprout of fabricated calamity—then the ancestral temples will be secure and officials and people blessed.
translations.idiomatic: He begged the emperor to establish Prince Jinyuan as great-grandson at once, ending doubt, ambition, and intrigue, and securing the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 臣備位宰相，不敢不盡言，惟陛下裁察。」

translations.literal: Your servant holds a place among chancellors and dares not fail to speak fully; may Your Majesty judge and examine."
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor he dared speak fully and asked the emperor to decide.

sentences.zh: 逾月，有詔起複皇孫金源郡王判大興尹，封原王。

translations.literal: After a month an edict ordered the great-grandson Prince Jinyuan to return to office as prefect of Daxing and enfeoffed him as Prince of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Prince Jinyuan was ordered back to serve as prefect of Daxing and enfeoffed as Prince of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 世宗諸子中趙王永中最長，其母張玄征女，玄征子汝弼為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Among Emperor Shizong's sons Prince Zhao Yongzhong was eldest; his mother was the daughter of Zhang Xuanzheng; Xuanzheng's son Rubi was Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao Yongzhong was the emperor's eldest son; his mother was Zhang Xuanzheng's daughter; Rubi was left vice director.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，世宗出汝弼為廣甯尹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the emperor sent Rubi out as Guangning Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-six the emperor posted Rubi to Guangning.

sentences.zh: 於是，左丞相守道致仕，遂以克寧為太尉，兼左丞相，原王為右丞相，因使克寧輔導之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Left Chancellor Shoudao retired, and Kening was made Grand Preceptor concurrently Left Chancellor; Prince of Yuan was made Right Chancellor, and Kening was made to guide and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Shoudao retired; Kening became grand preceptor and left chancellor; Prince of Yuan became right chancellor under Kening's guidance.

sentences.zh: 原王為丞相方四日，世宗問之曰：「汝治事幾日矣？」

translations.literal: Prince of Yuan had been chancellor only four days when the emperor asked him, "How many days have you handled affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Four days after Prince of Yuan became chancellor, the emperor asked how long he had been at work.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「四日。」

translations.literal: He answered, "Four days."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Four days."

sentences.zh: 「京尹與省事同乎？」

translations.literal: Is the capital prefect the same as the Secretariat affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Is the capital prefect's work the same as the Secretariat's?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「不同。」

translations.literal: He answered, "Not the same."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "No."

sentences.zh: 上笑曰：「京尹浩穰，尚書省總大體，所以不同也。」

translations.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "The capital prefecture is vast and populous; the Imperial Secretariat oversees the great frame—that is why they are not the same."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor laughed, "The capital is vast and the Secretariat sets policy—that is why they differ."

sentences.zh: 數日，複謂原王曰：「宮中有四方地圖，汝可觀之，知遠近厄塞也。」

translations.literal: Several days later he again told Prince of Yuan, "In the palace there is a map of the four directions; you may view it and know distance, peril, and strategic passes."
translations.idiomatic: Days later he told the prince to study the palace map of the realm and learn its distances and strategic passes.

sentences.zh: 世宗與宰相論錢幣，上曰：「中外皆患錢少，今京師積錢止五百萬貫，除屯兵路分其他郡縣錢可運至京師。」

translations.literal: The emperor discussed coinage with the chancellors and said, "Inside and outside all suffer from too little money; now the capital's accumulated coin is only five million strings; apart from garrison circuits, other prefectures' and counties' coin can be transported to the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Discussing coinage, the emperor said coin was scarce everywhere; the capital held only five million strings and he wished to draw in funds from the provinces.

sentences.zh: 克寧曰：「郡縣錢盡入京師，民間錢益少矣。

translations.literal: Kening said, "If all prefectural and county coin enters the capital, the people's coin will be even scarcer.
translations.idiomatic: Kening said moving all provincial coin to the capital would only make it scarcer among the people.

sentences.zh: 若起運其半，其半變折輕齎，庶幾錢貨流布也。」

translations.literal: If half is transported and half converted to light valuables for transport, perhaps currency can circulate."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed transporting half while converting half to light valuables so coin could circulate.

sentences.zh: 上嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and adopted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 章宗雖封原王，為丞相，克寧猶以未正太孫之位，屢請于世宗，世宗歎曰：「克寧，社稷之臣也。」

translations.literal: Although Zhangzong was enfeoffed Prince of Yuan and made chancellor, Kening because the great-grandson's place was not yet regular repeatedly petitioned Emperor Shizong; the emperor sighed and said, "Kening is a minister of the altars."
translations.idiomatic: Though Zhangzong was Prince of Yuan and chancellor, Kening kept pressing to regularize the great-grandson's status; the emperor called him a pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊午，宰相入見於香閣，既退，原王已出，克寧率宰臣屏左右奏立太孫，世宗許之。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day of the eleventh month the chancellors entered audience in the Fragrant Pavilion; after they withdrew Prince of Yuan had already left; Kening led the chief ministers, screened off attendants, and memorialized to establish the great-grandson; Emperor Shizong consented.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu of the eleventh month, after audience Kening had the ministers withdraw attendants and memorialized to establish the great-grandson; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 庚申，詔立原王右丞相為皇太孫。

translations.literal: On gengshen an edict established Prince of Yuan, right chancellor, as imperial great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Prince of Yuan was established as imperial great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 明日，徒單公弼尚息國公主納幣，賜六品以上宴于慶和殿。

translations.literal: The next day Tudan Gongbi, who had married Princess Xixi, presented betrothal gifts; a feast for officials of the sixth rank and above was given in the Qinghe Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Tudan Gongbi presented betrothal gifts and officials of the sixth rank and above feasted in the Qinghe Hall.

sentences.zh: 上謂諸王大臣曰：「太尉忠實明達，漢之周勃也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the princes and great ministers, "The Grand Preceptor is loyal, solid, clear, and penetrating—he is the Zhou Bo of Han."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the princes and ministers, "The Grand Preceptor is loyal and wise—Jin's Zhou Bo."

sentences.zh: 稱歎再三。

translations.literal: He praised him again and again.
translations.idiomatic: He praised him repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 克寧進酒，上舉觴為之酹。

translations.literal: Kening offered wine; the emperor raised his cup and poured a libation for him.
translations.idiomatic: Kening offered wine and the emperor poured a libation for him.

sentences.zh: 有詔給太尉假三日。

translations.literal: An edict granted the Grand Preceptor three days' leave.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted the Grand Preceptor three days' leave.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，複求解機務。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year he again requested to be relieved of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next first month he again asked to leave state affairs.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿遽求去邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Do you urgently wish to go?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Do you wish to leave so soon?

sentences.zh: 豈朕用卿有未盡乎？

translations.literal: Is it that in employing you I have not exhausted my use of you?
translations.idiomatic: Have I not used you fully?

sentences.zh: 或因喜怒用刑賞乎？

translations.literal: Or because of joy and anger in employing punishments and rewards?
translations.idiomatic: Or is it because of how I use punishments and rewards?

sentences.zh: 其他宰相未有能如卿者，宜勉留以輔朕。

translations.literal: No other chancellor has been able to be like you; you should strive to remain to assist me.
translations.idiomatic: No other chancellor equals you; stay and assist me.

sentences.zh: 卿若思念鄉土，可以一往，不必謝政事。

translations.literal: If you long for your native place you may go once—you need not resign from government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: If you miss home you may visit once without resigning office.

sentences.zh: 三月一日朕之生辰，卿不必到，從容至暑月還京師相見。」

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month, my birthday—you need not come; come at your ease by the summer month and we shall meet again in the capital."
translations.idiomatic: You need not come for my birthday on the third month's first day; return by summer and we shall meet."

sentences.zh: 四月，克寧還朝，入見上。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Kening returned to court and entered audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Kening returned and had audience.

sentences.zh: 上問曰：「卿往鄉中，百姓皆安業否？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked, "When you went to your native place, were the people all peacefully pursuing their livelihoods?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked whether the people were at peace in his homeland.

sentences.zh: 克寧曰：「生業頗安，然初起移至彼，未能滋殖耳。」

translations.literal: Kening said, "Their livelihoods are rather secure, but having just moved there at first they could not yet multiply and grow."
translations.idiomatic: Kening said they were fairly secure but, having just moved, had not yet fully prospered.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以丞相監修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was made chancellor supervising compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made supervising compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 上問史事，奏曰：「臣聞古者人君不觀史，願陛下勿觀。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked about historical affairs; he memorialized, "Your servant has heard that in antiquity rulers did not view the history; I hope Your Majesty will not view it."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about the histories, he said ancient rulers did not read them and asked the emperor not to read them either.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕豈欲觀此？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "How would I wish to view this?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said he had no wish to read them.

sentences.zh: 深知史事不詳，故問之耳。」

translations.literal: I deeply know historical affairs are not detailed, and therefore asked."
translations.idiomatic: He only asked because he knew the records were incomplete.

sentences.zh: 初，瀘溝河決久不能塞，加封安平侯，久之，水複故道。

translations.literal: Previously the Lugou River had burst its banks and long could not be blocked; he was additionally enfeoffed Marquis of Anping; after a long time the water returned to its old course.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lugou River long could not be diked, he was made Marquis of Anping; eventually the water returned to its course.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「鬼神雖不可窺測，即獲感應如此。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Though spirits cannot be fathomed, to obtain such responsive effect as this!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said even spirits could not be fathomed, yet the response was so clear.

sentences.zh: 克寧奏曰：「神之所佑者正也，人事乖，則弗享矣。

translations.literal: Kening memorialized, "What spirits aid is what is upright; if human affairs are perverse, they are not enjoyed.
translations.idiomatic: Kening said spirits aid what is upright; when human affairs go wrong, they receive no blessing.

sentences.zh: 報應之來皆由人事。」

translations.literal: Responsive effects all come from human affairs."
translations.idiomatic: All such responses come from human conduct.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 世宗頗信神仙浮圖之事，故克寧及之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong rather believed in immortals and Buddhist affairs; therefore Kening spoke to this.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong inclined toward immortals and Buddhism, so Kening spoke thus.

sentences.zh: 宋前主殂，宋主遣使進遺留物，上怪其禮物薄。

translations.literal: The former Song ruler died; the Song ruler sent envoys presenting leftover goods; the emperor found their gifts meager and wondered.
translations.idiomatic: When the former Song emperor died, the new emperor sent meager condolence gifts, which Shizong found odd.

sentences.zh: 克寧曰：「此非常貢，責之近於好利。」

translations.literal: Kening said, "This is not an ordinary tribute; to reprove them verges on coveting profit."
translations.idiomatic: Kening said this was not ordinary tribute and to reprove them would look greedy.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your words are right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃以其玉器五事、玻璃器大小二十事及茶器刀劍等還之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the five jade objects, twenty large and small glass vessels, and tea vessels, swords, and the like were returned.
translations.idiomatic: The jades, glassware, tea sets, swords, and the like were returned.

sentences.zh: 二十八年十一月癸丑，上幸克寧第。

translations.literal: On the guichou day of the eleventh month of the twenty-eighth year the emperor visited Kening's residence.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou of the eleventh month, year twenty-eight, the emperor visited Kening's home.

sentences.zh: 初，上欲以甲第賜克寧，克寧固辭，乃賜錢，因其舊居宏大之。

translations.literal: At first the emperor wished to grant him a first-rank mansion; Kening firmly declined; thereupon cash was granted and his old residence was enlarged.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had wished to give him a grand mansion; Kening declined, so cash was granted and his old house enlarged.

sentences.zh: 畢工，上臨幸，賜金器錦繡重彩，克寧亦有獻。

translations.literal: When construction was finished the emperor visited in person and granted gold vessels, brocade, and heavy silk; Kening also made offerings.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished the emperor visited, gave gold and silks, and Kening made offerings in return.

sentences.zh: 上飲歡甚，解禦衣以衣之。

translations.literal: The emperor drank in great joy and removed his imperial robe to clothe him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drank happily and gave Kening his own robe.

sentences.zh: 詔畫克寧像藏內府。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Kening's portrait painted and stored in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his portrait painted for the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙亥，世宗不豫。

translations.literal: On the yihai day of the twelfth month Emperor Shizong fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai of the twelfth month the emperor fell ill.

sentences.zh: 甲申，克寧率宰執入問起居。

translations.literal: On jiashen Kening led the chief ministers to enter and inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Kening led the ministers to inquire after his health.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕疾殆矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "My illness is nearly fatal."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "My illness is nearly fatal."

sentences.zh: 謂克寧曰：「皇太孫年雖弱冠，生而明達，卿等竭力輔之。」

translations.literal: He said to Kening, "The imperial great-grandson, though weak in years, was born clear and penetrating; you and the others must assist him with all your strength."
translations.idiomatic: He told Kening, "The great-grandson is young but bright; assist him with all your strength."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「尚書省政務權聽于皇太孫。」

translations.literal: He also said, "The administrative affairs of the Imperial Secretariat are temporarily to be heard by the imperial great-grandson."
translations.idiomatic: He also said Secretariat affairs should temporarily be heard by the great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 克寧奏曰：「陛下幸上京時，宣孝太子守國，許除六品以下官，今可權行也。」

translations.literal: Kening memorialized, "When Your Majesty visited the Upper Capital, the late Xuanxiao crown prince guarded the state and was permitted to appoint officials below the sixth rank; now this may be done provisionally."
translations.idiomatic: Kening said the crown prince had once been allowed to appoint officials below the sixth rank and the great-grandson might do the same.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「五品以下亦何不可。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Why can those below the fifth rank not also?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said officials below the fifth rank might also be appointed.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，詔皇太孫攝行政事，注授五品以下官。

translations.literal: On yiyou an edict ordered the imperial great-grandson to administer government affairs and appoint officials below the fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou the great-grandson was ordered to govern and appoint officials below the fifth rank.

sentences.zh: 詔太孫與諸王大臣俱宿禁中。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the great-grandson and the princes and great ministers all to lodge within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: The great-grandson, princes, and ministers were ordered to lodge in the palace.

sentences.zh: 克寧奏曰：「皇太孫與諸王宜別嫌疑，正名分，宿止同處，禮有未安。」

translations.literal: Kening memorialized, "The imperial great-grandson and the princes should separate suspicion and rectify names; lodging together—the ritual is not secure."
translations.idiomatic: Kening said the great-grandson and princes should observe proper separation and not lodge together.

sentences.zh: 詔太孫居慶和殿東廡。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the great-grandson to lodge in the eastern wing of the Qinghe Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The great-grandson was lodged in the eastern wing of the Qinghe Hall.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，詔克寧以太尉兼尚書令，封延安郡王。

translations.literal: On bingxu an edict made Kening Grand Preceptor concurrently Director of the Imperial Secretariat and enfeoffed him Duke of Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Kening was made grand preceptor and director of the Imperial Secretariat and enfeoffed Duke of Yan'an.

sentences.zh: 平章政事襄為右丞相，右丞張汝霖為平章政事。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Xiang became Right Chancellor; Right Vice Director Zhang Rulin became Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang became right chancellor and Zhang Rulin grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 戊子，詔克寧、襄、汝霖宿於內殿。

translations.literal: On wuzi an edict ordered Kening, Xiang, and Rulin to lodge in the inner hall.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Kening, Xiang, and Rulin were ordered to lodge in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 二十九年正月癸巳，世宗崩于福安殿。

translations.literal: On the guisi day of the first month of the twenty-ninth year Emperor Shizong died in the Fu'an Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi of the first month, year twenty-nine, Emperor Shizong died in the Fu'an Hall.

sentences.zh: 是日，克寧等宣遺詔，立皇太孫為皇帝，是為章宗。

translations.literal: That day Kening and the others proclaimed the testamentary edict and established the imperial great-grandson as emperor—this was Emperor Zhangzong.
translations.idiomatic: That day Kening proclaimed the testamentary edict and established the great-grandson as emperor—Emperor Zhangzong.

sentences.zh: 徙封為東平郡王。

translations.literal: He was transferred in enfeoffment to Prince of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 詔克寧朝朔望，朝日設坐殿上。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Kening to attend court on the first and fifteenth of the month; on court days a seat was set for him in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: An edict required Kening to attend on the first and fifteenth; on court days a seat was set for him in the hall.

sentences.zh: 克寧固辭，詔近臣勉諭。

translations.literal: Kening firmly declined; an edict ordered close attendants to encourage and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: Kening firmly declined; close attendants were ordered to persuade him.

sentences.zh: 克寧涕泣謝曰：「憐憫老臣，倖免常朝，豈敢當坐禮。」

translations.literal: Kening wept and thanked him, saying, "In pity for this old minister I am fortunately exempted from regular court—how dare I accept the seated ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, he thanked the emperor: "You spare an old man regular court—how dare I take a seat?"

sentences.zh: 其後，每朝必為克寧設坐，克寧侍立益敬。

translations.literal: Afterward, at every court a seat was set for Kening, and Kening stood attending even more respectfully.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward a seat was always set for him, yet Kening stood by even more respectfully.

sentences.zh: 即位詔文「凡除名開落官吏並量材錄用」，張汝霖奏真盜枉法不可恕，克寧曰：「陛下初即位，行非常之典，贓吏誤沾恩宥其害小，國之大信不可失也。」

translations.literal: In the accession edict it said, "All dismissed and demoted officials are to be employed according to talent"; Zhang Rulin memorialized that true thieves who perverted the law could not be forgiven; Kening said, "Your Majesty has just ascended and is enacting an extraordinary measure; if corrupt officials mistakenly receive grace the harm is small, but the great trust of the state cannot be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rulin argued corrupt officials should not be pardoned; Kening said the new emperor's amnesty must not break the state's great trust for the sake of minor harm.

sentences.zh: 章宗深然之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhangzong deeply approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 無何，進拜太傅，兼尚書令，賜尚衣玉帶。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Grand Tutor, concurrently Director of the Imperial Secretariat, and granted the imperial robe and jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand tutor and director of the Imperial Secretariat and given the imperial robe and jade belt.

sentences.zh: 乞致仕，不許。

translations.literal: He requested retirement but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire but was refused.

sentences.zh: 詔譯《諸葛孔明傳》賜之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the translation of the Biography of Zhuge Kongming presented to him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Biography of Zhuge Liang translated and presented to him.

sentences.zh: 詔尚書省曰：「太傅年高，旬休外四日一居休，大事錄之，細事不須親也。」

translations.literal: An edict to the Imperial Secretariat said, "The Grand Tutor is advanced in years; apart from the ten-day rest each month, rest one day in four; record great affairs; small affairs need not be handled in person."
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was told the Grand Tutor should rest one day in four besides regular leave, handle only great affairs in person, and leave small matters to others.

sentences.zh: 賜金五百兩、銀五千兩、錢千萬、重彩二百端、絹二千匹。

translations.literal: He was granted five hundred taels of gold, five thousand taels of silver, ten million strings of cash, two hundred bolts of heavy silk, and two thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He received five hundred taels of gold, five thousand of silver, ten million strings of cash, and lavish silks.

sentences.zh: 尚書省奏猛安謀克願試進士者聽之，上曰：「其應襲猛安謀克者學於太學可乎？」

translations.literal: The Imperial Secretariat memorialized that military colonists who wished to try for the jinshi examination should be permitted; the emperor said, "For those who should inherit military colonies, is study in the Imperial University acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat proposed letting military colonists take the jinshi exam, the emperor asked whether heirs to military colonies should study at the Imperial University instead.

sentences.zh: 克寧曰：「承平日久，今之猛安謀克其材武已不及前輩，萬一有警，使誰禦之？

translations.literal: Kening said, "In long peace the military colonists of today in martial talent already cannot match their predecessors; if perchance there is an alarm, with whom will we defend?
translations.idiomatic: Kening said that in long peace today's colonists lacked their forebears' martial skill—if alarm came, who would defend the realm?

sentences.zh: 習辭藝，忘武備，于國弗便。」

translations.literal: To study literary arts and forget military preparedness is not convenient for the state."
translations.idiomatic: To study letters and forget arms was bad for the state.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「太傅言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "The Grand Tutor's words are right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed with the Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 章宗初即位，頗好辭章，而疆埸方有事，故克寧言及之。

translations.literal: When Zhangzong first ascended he rather loved literary composition, while the frontier just then had affairs; therefore Kening spoke to this.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzong at first loved literature while the frontier was troubled, so Kening spoke to this.

sentences.zh: 明昌二年，克寧屬疾，章宗往視之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Mingchang Kening fell ill; Zhangzong went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Mingchang Kening fell ill and Zhangzong visited him.

sentences.zh: 克寧頓首謝曰：「臣無似，嘗蒙先帝任使，陛下即位，屬以上相，今臣老病，將先犬馬填溝壑，無以輔明主綏四方。

translations.literal: Kening bowed his head and thanked him, saying, "Your servant is unworthy; I once received appointment by the late emperor; when Your Majesty ascended I was entrusted as chief minister; now I am old and ill and will precede my dogs and horses in filling gullies and ravines—I cannot assist the enlightened ruler in pacifying the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Kening bowed and said he had served the late emperor and Zhangzong as chief minister, but was old and ill and could no longer aid the throne.

sentences.zh: 陛下念臣駑怯，親枉車駕臨幸，死有餘罪矣。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty thinks of your servant's dull timidity and personally bends your carriage to visit—death would still leave guilt."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's visit, he said, shamed one who deserved death even without it.

sentences.zh: 是日，即榻前拜太師，封淄王，加賜甚厚。

translations.literal: That day, before the couch he was appointed Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed Prince of Zi, and additional gifts were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: That day, at his bedside, he was made Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed Prince of Zi, and richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 是歲二月，薨，遺表，其大概言：「人君往往重君子而反疏之，輕小人而終昵之。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year he died; his final memorial in general said, "Rulers often value gentlemen yet in the end keep them at a distance, and slight petty men yet in the end draw them close.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month, leaving a final memorial warning that rulers often honor gentlemen yet distance them and slight petty men yet keep them close.

sentences.zh: 願陛下慎終如始，安不忘危，而言不及私。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will be careful at the end as at the beginning, secure yet not forget peril, and that my words do not touch on private interest."
translations.idiomatic: He urged the emperor to be as careful at the end as at the beginning, secure yet not forget danger, and spoke without private interest.

sentences.zh: 詔有司護喪事，歸葬於萊州，諡曰忠烈。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to conduct the funeral; he was returned for burial in Laizhou; his posthumous title was Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were ordered to conduct his funeral; he was buried in Laizhou with the posthumous name Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 明 昌五年，配享世宗廟廷，圖像衍慶宮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Mingchang he was paired in sacrifice in Emperor Shizong's temple hall; his portrait was placed in the Yanging Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Mingchang he was enshrined in Shizong's temple and his portrait placed in the Yanging Palace.

sentences.zh: 大安元年，改配享章宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Da'an he was changed to paired sacrifice in Emperor Zhangzong's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Da'an he was moved to Zhangzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：徒單克寧可謂大臣矣，功高而身愈下，位盛而心愈勞。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Tudan Kening may be called a great minister; merit high yet the person ever lower, position flourishing yet the heart ever more toiling.
translations.idiomatic: In summary: Tudan Kening was a great minister—his merit rose while he lowered himself, his rank grew while he toiled more.

sentences.zh: 《經》曰：「在上不驕，高而不危，制節謹度，滿而不溢」，所以長守富貴。

translations.literal: The Classic says, "In high place without arrogance, high yet not perilous, regulating measure and careful in degree, full yet not overflowing"—by this one long preserves wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says that those who are high yet not arrogant, full yet not overflowing, long preserve wealth and honor.

sentences.zh: 故曰忠信匪懈，不施其功，履盛滿而不忘，德之上也。

translations.literal: Thus loyal faith without slackness, not displaying merit, treading fullness without forgetting—this is virtue at its height.
translations.idiomatic: Thus loyal faith without slackness, not parading merit, remembering fullness without pride—that is the highest virtue.

sentences.zh: 孜孜勉勉，恪守職業，不居不可成，不事不可行，人主知之，次也。

translations.literal: Diligent and striving, strictly keeping one's office, not occupying what cannot be accomplished, not undertaking what cannot be done—when the ruler knows this, it is next.
translations.idiomatic: Diligently keeping one's office, attempting only what can succeed—when the ruler knows this, it is next in rank.

sentences.zh: 諫期必行，言期必聽，為其事必有其功者，又其次也。

translations.literal: Remonstrance expected to be carried out, words expected to be heard, doing the affair and necessarily having achievement—this is again lower.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance that must be followed, counsel that must be heard, and deeds that must succeed—this is lower still.
